About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic is expanding its reseller program in Japan and Korea.

As our Reseller Operations Manager for Japan and Korea, you'll own how resellers in both countries get onboarded, transact, get paid, and get supported, across both of our resale motions: hyperscaler resale, where partners resell Claude through the cloud marketplaces (AWS Bedrock today, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry to follow), and direct resale, where partners resell on Anthropic paper through our own quote-to-order and billing systems.

The global team builds the program; you make it work for Japanese and Korean partners and feed back what has to change.
This is an operator role, not a partner manager role. In the first months you'll be validating deal registrations and answering partner tickets yourself; by the end of the first year the volume should be running on documented process, service levels, and vendor or system coverage that you set up.

Own reseller onboarding for Japan and Korea end to end: application intake, screening coordination, agreement execution, marketplace authorization, entitlement setup, and activation, and keep the partner record in Salesforce decision-grade for both regions.
Run hyperscaler (3P) reseller operations: deal-registration intake and validation within SLA, marketplace authorizations and private-offer processing with the cloud alliance teams, and end-customer reporting on every reseller transaction so partner-sourced revenue can be attributed.
Run direct (1P) reseller operations: partner quotes and order forms, order booking and provisioning, and commit tracking and true-ups with Deal Desk, RevOps, and Accounting, and work with Finance and Tax on local invoicing, currency, and consumption-tax handling for each transaction route.
Run the regional side of reseller incentives: eligibility, validation of quarterly payouts, and partner disputes, in partnership with the global incentive operations team and Finance.
Stand up first-line operational support for resellers in Japanese and Korean during local business hours, inside the global partner support queue rather than alongside it, and localize the onboarding, deal-registration, and ordering content partners depend on.
Manage any outsourced or contracted operations capacity used in region (scope, quality, service levels) and coordinate with Enablement on the logistics of local-language certification and training.
Own reseller reporting for Japan and Korea: registration volume and cycle time, activation, attach, and attributed revenue by partner and by motion, and use it to tell the regional teams and the global program what to fix next.
Adopt the global Partner Operations playbooks where they fit, write the in-region variants where they don't, and represent Japan and Korea requirements in partner systems and automation work so manual volume doesn't grow with partner count.

Several years in channel, reseller, distribution, or partner operations at a technology company, ideally touching both a cloud-marketplace motion and a direct or contract-based resale motion.
Working proficiency in Japanese, Korean, and English. You'll run operational relationships with partners in both countries and work daily with a US-based team; proficiency doesn't need to be identical across all three, but you need to be able to work with partners in both regions.
Practical knowledge of how at least one major cloud marketplace's reseller program works (authorizations, private offers, deal registration), or deep experience in one motion and a track record of picking up the other quickly.
Hands-on experience with quote-to-order, order management, or partner billing, and the Finance, Deal Desk, and Legal coordination that comes with it.
A track record of taking a manual process and turning it into documented workflow, service levels, and reporting, including managing vendors or contractors who execute part of it.
Hands-on Salesforce experience (reporting, data maintenance), and comfort being the only operations person in the region while working with a team many time zones away.

Experience inside the Japanese or Korean enterprise reseller and systems-integrator ecosystem, including local invoicing, credit, and consumption-tax conventions.
Experience with partner incentive or rebate operations, or with a partner program during its launch phase.
Experience with PRM or deal-registration tooling, or building automations with Claude or similar tools to run operational workflows at volume.

s.h: How this role works with the team
s.t:
You'll report into Partner Experience and work day to day with two groups.

The global Partner Operations team in San Francisco owns the reseller program's systems, and playbooks; our reseller operations owner there is your direct counterpart, and you'll split work along a simple line: they own the global process, you own its execution and adaptation in Japan and Korea.

The Japan and Korea go-to-market teams own the partner relationships and the commercial conversations; you're the operational layer underneath them, and the person they come to when something about a partner's onboarding, order, or payout needs to move.

You'll also be the regional voice into Finance, Deal Desk, RevOps, and the cloud alliance teams on anything that has to work differently in these markets.

The North America Revenue Strategy & Operations team is the operational engine behind Celonis’s go-to-market success in our highest-potential market.

By unifying operations, analytics, and reporting infrastructure into a single, consistent model, the team eliminates friction, drives alignment, and gives our GTM organizations the data-driven foundation they need to scale.

This role sits on the Revenue Strategy & Operations team as a dedicated business partner to North America Sales leadership — embedding with Regional Vice Presidents and their teams to bring operational rigor, clean data, and a steady cadence to how the field runs.

Based in our Raleigh hub, you are the Strategy & Operations business partner to a portfolio of North America Sales leaders — three Regional Vice Presidents (RVPs) plus at least one adjacent GTM leader — and their teams. You’ll operate alongside a peer Strategy & Operations Manager, splitting coverage of the six-RVP NAM Sales leadership team between you so that every leader has a dedicated operator in their corner.
It’s a hands-on, high-impact role: you own the forecast and pipeline cadence for your leaders, turn scattered inputs into a clear and reliable operating picture, and sit shoulder-to-shoulder with RVPs, Sales Directors (SD), and VP+ leaders every week.

You’ll be mentored by senior operations leaders as you take ownership, and you’ll help the function get smarter over time by leveraging AI GTM capabilities to make recurring work faster, more scalable, and simpler for the field Account Executives (AEs) — unlocking real productivity gains.
The work you’ll do
Be the business partner: Serve as the dedicated Strategy & Operations partner to your portfolio of NAM Sales leaders — and their teams.
Own the forecast and pipeline cadence: Run the weekly forecast, pipeline inspection, and deal-review rhythm with your leaders; ensure roll-ups are accurate, risk-adjusted, and decision-ready for RVP and VP+ reviews.
Drive pipeline health and hygiene: Inspect pipeline coverage, stage progression, and qualification rigor (MEDDPICC); surface gaps, aging, and slippage early, and partner with leaders and Account Executives (AEs) on the actions to close them.
Enable planning and capacity: Support territory, quota, capacity, and headcount planning for your teams; model coverage scenarios and translate them into clean, executable plans.
Prepare leadership reporting and QBRs: Build the recurring reporting packages, scorecards, and QBR narratives your leaders rely on, pulling structured data from Salesforce and internal tools into decision-ready outputs.
Operate AI-native: Leverage AI GTM capabilities and agentic workflows to automate recurring reporting, accelerate deal and pipeline inspection, and make common analytical asks self-serve — simplifying how the field works and unlocking productivity.
Lead strategic initiatives: Partner on and help lead select strategic initiatives and planning workstreams for your coverage area, from framing the problem through execution and measured outcomes.
Build tight interlocks: Partner closely with your peer S&O Manager and the broader NAM & Global RevOps teams to keep the operating model consistent across the leadership bench, and collaborate on holistic initiatives spanning Sales, BDR, Partner, and Value Engineering.

Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy.

Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

The Sr. Business Operations Manager is a strategic partner to the leadership of Samsara’s Global Support organization, driving operational excellence and enabling data-informed decision-making at scale. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, supporting senior leadership with the insights, communications, and operational frameworks needed to run and grow the business effectively.
This role owns the annual operating plan and the operating cadence that measures performance against it.

On the planning side, you will own the capacity, headcount, and cost model that connects support volume, productivity, AI deflection, and staffing assumptions into a defensible operating plan — and act as the connective tissue between Support leadership, Workforce Management, and Finance.

On the business operations side, you will own the reporting and business review cadence for Customer Support, turning a wide set of operational metrics into a clear narrative about what is happening, why, and what leadership should do about it.
This is a high-autonomy role for a builder. You will take ambiguous, loosely scoped problems: a cost target, a capacity gap, an unexplained trend, and return with structured analysis, a defensible model, and a recommendation leaders can act on.

You will operate credibly with senior stakeholders across Support, Finance, and People, influence without direct authority, and use modern AI tools every day to work at a level of speed and rigor that would not otherwise be possible.

Success in this role looks like leaders making better decisions faster, with a plan and a set of numbers everyone trusts.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

Own the annual operating plan (AOP) for the Support organization end to end: building and maintaining the capacity, headcount, and cost model that translates volume forecasts, productivity, AI deflection, and staffing assumptions into a defensible operating plan and budget.
Model and pressure-test the strategic levers available to the business: headcount and vendor/BPO mix, cost to serve, deflection and automation impact, service level and coverage tradeoffs — and bring leadership clear recommendations with quantified impact and stated assumptions.
Own the Customer Support business review cadence (monthly and quarterly reviews) end to end: metric definition and data validation, executive narrative and insight, and follow-through on the decisions and actions that come out of it.
Build and maintain the reporting frameworks and metric definitions leaders run the business on — productivity, cost to serve, CSAT, time to resolution, deflection — and make them self-serve so managers can answer their own questions.
Partner with Support leaders on the operating programs that turn plan into behavior, including productivity and incentive program design, capacity allocation, and operational improvement initiatives that measurably improve efficiency and customer experience.
Leverage AI tools (e.g., Claude) and self-service data capabilities on a day-to-day basis to accelerate modeling, analysis, narrative generation, and reporting — and raise the bar for how the broader operations team applies them.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

10+ years of experience in business operations, strategic finance/FP&A, management consulting, strategy, or a related field.
Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year accredited university.
Experience owning an annual operating plan, capacity plan, or equivalent multi-quarter planning process for a large organization or function.
Demonstrated experience building and owning complex operating or financial models (headcount, capacity, and cost) that senior leaders make decisions from.
Experience owning a recurring executive business review cadence (e.g., MBR/QBR) end to end, including metric definitions, narrative, and follow-through.
Demonstrated ability to build executive-level presentations and strategic communications that convey a clear, compelling narrative.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to independently source, interpret, and synthesize large and imperfect datasets to support decision-making, including familiarity with data tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker, SQL, Databricks) for self-serve analytics.
Comfort and previous experience using AI tools for analysis, modeling, content generation, and workflow automation.
Experience working cross-functionally and influencing senior stakeholders without direct authority.
High degree of independence and intellectual curiosity: able to take a loosely defined problem and return with structured, rigorous thinking and actionable recommendations.
Experience in or with a customer support, technical support, or service delivery organization operating at scale across multiple sites and a vendor/BPO mix.

Description
The Clinical Operations Manager is responsible for the day-to-day management of an assigned team of both permanent and contracted staff (e.g., Clinical Research Associates (CRA)/(cCRA)) and other Clinical Operations Support personnel) overseeing their performance and training, ensuring adequate monitoring and support team resources, allocating resources to projects, identifying quality issues related to Clinical Operations activities and establishing action plans to address them.

s.h: More specifically, the Clinical Operations Manager must
s.t:
Ensure that clinical monitoring activities of their assigned team are performed to the Sponsor’s satisfaction, ensuring timely quality deliverables, within budget, and in accordance with applicable standard operating procedures (SOPs), regulations, good clinical practices, and study-specific requirements.
Oversee the performance of their direct reports, ensuring they are meeting performance objectives and taking appropriate remedial actions as required. Implement professional development and performance evaluations.
Support the training and development of Clinical Operations personnel within their remit, providing coaching and mentoring. Ensure team members’ consistent use of study tools and training materials.
Assist in developing and delivering training for Clinical Operations personnel.
Track Clinical Operations metrics and monitor adherence to targets (e.g., number of site visits performed, utilization, and timeliness to complete deliverables such as site visit report finalization, follow-up letters, timesheets, expense reports and required training.)
Ensure monitoring expenses are compliant with policy and aligned with established guidelines.
Perform Quality Assessment Visits (QAV) with CRAs.
Identify quality issues related to Clinical Operations activities through project meetings, site and team communications, site visit reports and follow-up letters, QAVs, and quality assurance audit findings. Summarize findings and establish action plans to bring corrective actions.
Serve as a point of contact for Clinical Operations personnel and other team members for assigned projects or initiatives.
Serve as a management contact for sites, project teams, and sponsors when issues related to Clinical Operations and trial management activities must be escalated to ensure communication is maintained and resolution is achieved.
Assist with assessing and interviewing potential Clinical Operations candidates.
Drive innovation within Clinical Operations by identifying opportunities to optimize workflows and enhance efficiency, quality, and scalability, while supporting the adoption of emerging technologies and AI-enabled solutions to improve study execution.
Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and proactive problem-solving across Clinical Operations teams.
May conduct on-site or remote monitoring visits to offer support to project teams.
May perform site visit report review and track site visit report metrics to ensure compliance.
May review or provide input to Clinical Operations plans and tools.
May review and provide feedback on related SOPs and Tools during updates.
May support site survey activities to assess site satisfaction and synthesize insights in support of continuous improvement.
Employee may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.
Our company
The work environment
At Indero , you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are integrity, commitment and teamwork. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.
As a Clinical Operations Manager, you will be eligible for the following perks:
Flexible work schedule
Permanent full-time position
Complete benefits (medical, dental, vision, RRSP, vacation, personal days, virtual medical clinic, public transportation rebates, social activities)
Ongoing learning and development
About Indero
Indero is a contract research organization (CRO) specialized in dermatology with a team of over 350 employees. Since its beginnings in 2000, our organization has benefited from a solid reputation for the quality of its research and services exceeding the expectations of its clients. Based in Montreal, Indero continues to grow and expand in North America.

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations.

Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide.

Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

We have hubs in the Bay Area, NYC, Austin, Toronto, and São Paulo. However, we maintain a remote-first work culture. #WorkFromAnywhere
We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.
We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

Remote - Mexico City, Mexico
From Home / Beach / Mountain / Cafe / Anywhere!
We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed team. So you can find your productive zone and work from there.

Sardine is rapidly acquiring new customers and executing on an ambitious roadmap. Reporting directly to the Global Head of Expansion, the General Manager - Mexico will own Sardine's market strategy, revenue growth, and customer success in Mexico.

This person will partner cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, Product, Account Management, and Partnerships to establish Sardine as the leading fraud prevention platform in the market, build strategic relationships with banks and payment networks, and represent the voice of Mexican customers within the broader organization.

Market Strategy & Entry
Define and prioritize Mexico market entry and expansion priorities based on regulatory readiness, fraud landscape, and addressable market size.
Partner with regional Sales, Marketing, Product, and Account Management leaders to develop market-specific strategies aligned to Mexico's financial infrastructure and compliance environment.
Influence regional organizational planning and support hiring as the Mexico business scales.
Revenue & Pipeline
Own Mexico's ARR and new logo targets, partnering with regional Sales leadership on execution while holding accountability for market-level attainment — supporting strategic opportunities, shaping market strategy, and providing fraud expertise throughout the sales cycle
GTM Strategy
Influence regional GTM strategy in partnership with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Partnerships, and Product. Leverage Sardine's Sonar consortium network as a differentiator in prospect and partner conversations.
Establish operational playbooks for how Sardine enters, scales, and retains customers in Mexico.
Develop strategic relationships with Mexican banks, payment networks (e.g., SPEI, CoDi), and system integrators to accelerate distribution and reduce time-to-revenue in the market.
Customer Success & Retention
Partner with Account Management on strategic enterprise accounts, executive business reviews, and expansion opportunities.
Represent the voice of Mexican customers by translating customer feedback, fraud trends, and regional requirements into product and market strategy.

8+ years of experience in a GTM, general management, or leadership role within fintech, payments, or fraud/risk technology, ideally with direct exposure to the Mexican market.
Established network of relationships with banks, payment networks, regulators, and system integrators in Mexico.
Proven track record of driving revenue growth and building go-to-market strategy in a new or scaling market.
Deep understanding of Mexico's regulatory, compliance, and fraud landscape.
Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with experience partnering across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success.
Fluent in Spanish and English; willingness to travel within the region as needed.

We are seeking a dedicated and enthusiastic candidate to provide exceptional Customer service management to the Airbnb community as a Partner Operations Manager, Mandarin . The Partner Operations Manager, Mandarin is supporting the global Delivery function by driving partner and service performance. Accountable and responsible for the holistic performance of a partner or service or languageEnable and oversee a strong operational environment for your partners and services and ensure high quality support for the community from your partners
Set up for success your partner / service to deliver exceptional quality support to our community
Prioritise high impact focus areas with your partner/service in line with the company strategy
Actively work with core internal functions such as Quality, Workforce planning, Training to understand insights on performance and based on them, action within your partner / service
Act as a single point of contact, representing your partner / service across Delivery and CS
Present & report up on performance & progress to leadership across Delivery and CS
Hold partners accountable for the delivery of Airbnb goals
Own end to end the operationalization and successful adoption of new initiatives, projects and changes that impact your partner or service or language
Ensure alignment with Global CS Delivery
Input collectively with other ROMs to Sr Management and into the global delivery business reviews to provide a complete performance narrative to our leadership
Collaborate with your peers to ensure consistency & scalability in Global Delivery
Support and drive strategic initiatives within Delivery and your service
Identify and drive partner and service level continuous improvement opportunities that enhance performance, both day to day tactical and strategic forward looking
Collect feedback and be the voice of our community and partners to improve performance and optimize processes for the partner, service and global community
As required, collaborate with and understand the needs of your regional market and provide support to market managers and local business operations.
Collaborate with internal function such as BPI, PMO, Product on the launch of initiatives, projects and changes to bring improvements to your partner or service and mitigate potential risks

Your background & experience
A minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in a customer service or an operations role with 5+ years in a partner management, BPO environment
Demonstrable experience in driving improved performance as a partner/Regional Operations manager
Experience in the deployment of resources to manage real-time crisis situations, including managing high severity/sensitivity cases and decision-making authority for losses
Experience in data analysis and reporting to identify performance trends, as well as developing and implementing performance management standards
Demonstrable experience translating big picture goals and strategy into implementable and concrete actions for your partners
Ability to work weekend days and on-call required
Able to travel in Europe, APAC and NA when required
Your skills & expertise
Exceptional partner and stakeholder management - In depth understanding of business process outsourcing at scale, holding partners accountable for their performance and prioritizing the high impact areas
Exceptional performance management at scale - setting clear goals, expectations and actions while continuously driving success metrics
Strong data driven decision making with root cause analysis - ability to understand the data to derive to objective decisions
Strong communication, data driven storytelling and influencing skills - to present to leadership and collaborate with different stakeholders and manage time sensitive situations, while remaining calm and poised under pressure
Organized, structured and resourceful - able to juggle and multi-task, with an attention to detail and follow through even in ambiguous situations
Strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities at scale - to evaluate procedures and identify opportunities for improvement
Strong proficiency in various data analysis and reporting tools to track performance trends (tableau, salesforce, SQL, Excel, Google Sheets, etc.)

EBANX is one of the most successful fintechs to emerge from Latin America — and today, we are building a truly global payments company. Our mission has remained constant from day one: to unlock access and enable companies and consumers to participate in the digital economy, no matter where they are.
What started as a bold vision has grown into a platform that connects some of the world’s largest digital businesses with customers across 21 of the fastest-growing markets. We operate where complexity exists — turning local challenges into global opportunities and building the infrastructure that allows payments to move further, faster, and smarter.
We are a team of builders and problem-solvers. We think globally, act with curiosity, and believe diversity of thought is a competitive advantage.
As EBANX enters its next phase of hyper growth, we are looking for people who want to shape the future of payments, expand what’s possible, and help connect businesses and consumers across borders.
Let’s build what’s next — together.

s.h: What your day-to-day will look like
s.t:
Lead the identification, analysis, and prioritization of strategic initiatives to significantly improve payment authorization rates and overall payment performance.
Design and implement advanced analytical models to predict payment declines, identify their root causes, and recommend preventive actions.
Own end-to-end payment optimization projects, from opportunity assessment and prioritization through implementation and post-launch performance analysis.

Reports to: Sales Operations Manager
Job purpose: Support the administration, calculation, and reconciliation of sales compensation across a fast-growing global SaaS sales organization. Own the monthly mechanics that keep sellers paid accurately and on time, while helping build new processes, including bookings reconciliation and contract automation, as the team and the business scale.
Employment type: Permanent, full-time.
Locations: Must be based in the Atlanta, GA area. This is a hybrid role, with occasional in-person meetings in the Atlanta office.

What We Do
RELEX runs the planning decisions behind 600+ retailers and manufacturers worldwide, deciding, at real scale, what gets forecast, stocked, priced, promoted, and produced across the entire value chain.

Few problems combine this much data, this much complexity, and this much real-world weight: get it right and a shelf stays stocked, a factory line doesn’t stall, food doesn’t spoil in a warehouse before it’s sold. Get it wrong, and it shows up in actual losses, for some of the largest retail and manufacturing brands in the world.
We’ve grown for 76 consecutive quarters straight, and it’s still accelerating. The first half of 2026 was the strongest in the company’s history. We’re a team of 2,000+ people, headquartered in Helsinki, with offices across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific.
In response to our fast growth and market expansion, we are looking for ...
What we need you to do and be
Calculate monthly sales commissions, process manual adjustments, and maintain accurate crediting records across the sales organization.
Conduct crediting reviews and periodic audits, catching and resolving discrepancies before they reach the field.
Coordinate with Payroll to ensure commission payments are processed accurately and on schedule each cycle.
Investigate and resolve compensation disputes raised by sellers and managers, escalating complex cases where needed.
Administer and maintain our sales compensation platform, keeping calculations, adjustments, and records current and reliable. This includes improving the platform's UI and the seller experience so sellers see only what's relevant to their own commissions, driving transparency and adoption across the field.
Lead the rollout of a contracts platform into the deal-closing motion, including configuration and automation that connects signed contracts to the compensation and booking process.
Design and formalize a bookings review and reconciliation process, partnering with Finance to validate the bookable figures that drive seller payouts.
Serve as a first line of support for sellers, fielding and resolving questions on payments, timing, and crediting.
Document new processes as they take shape, building a clear reference for the team as compensation administration scales with the business.

This is a broad, hands-on role at the centre of the People Team, and the first point of contact for colleagues in London and across Europe. Around half your time goes on core People Operations: systems, records, documentation and the employee lifecycle. A quarter is spent advising managers and employees on everyday employee relations matters.

The remaining quarter supports Workplace Experience: keeping our London office running well and helping deliver events people actually want to come to. This role is hybrid and requires presence on-site for 3 days a week in our London office in Moorgate.
It suits someone who enjoys variety and is equally comfortable handling a sensitive ER case in the morning, cleaning up HRIS data in the afternoon, and setting up for an all-hands the next day. You will get exposure across the whole People function and the chance to contribute real deliverables from day one. Here’s how you’ll contribute:
People Operations
Be the first point of contact for employee queries, resolving them through our case management system or pointing people to the information they need.
Maintain our People Systems, keeping people records accurate, delivering timely data to Payroll, and meeting government and legal compliance requirements.
Maintain HR documentation, including personnel files in hard copy, shared drives and the HRIS; create and distribute contracts, letters and employment confirmations.
Own the administrative side of the employee lifecycle: offers, contracts, onboarding, changes, family leave and leavers.
Coordinate onboarding so new joiners have everything they need to succeed on their first day, and run Day 1 Orientation for London starters.
Track spend against People budgets and support purchasing, vendor set-up and invoice processing.
Partner with teams across the People organisation to deliver projects, improve processes and drive efficiencies in areas such as learning and development, career growth, performance management, employer branding and communications, wellbeing and mental health, and diversity and inclusion.
Leverage AI tools to speed up routine drafting, summarising and tracking, while maintaining strong judgement around accuracy and confidentiality.
Employee Relations and Advisory
Act as first-line advisor on employee relations matters: absence and sickness, probation, flexible working requests, performance concerns, grievances and disciplinaries. You’ll triage cases and handle straightforward ones end to end.
Own the ER case log: record every case, track it through to resolution, and keep notes and documentation to an audit-ready standard.
Prepare ER documentation such as invite letters, outcome letters and settlement paperwork, and take minutes at formal hearings.
Coach line managers through everyday people conversations, escalating complex, high-risk or multi-jurisdiction cases to the People Partner.
Provide Tier 1 policy interpretation, applying UK employment law and Scandit policy consistently and fairly.
Spot patterns across cases and flag recurring themes to the People Partner so we fix causes, not just symptoms.
Support policy work, drafting and reviewing policies, keeping the handbook current, and helping roll out changes with clear guidance for managers.
Workplace Experience and Events
Keep the WeWork London office running smoothly: supplies, kitchen stock, non-IT equipment, shared spaces and equipment, all in line with health and safety standards.
Coordinate in-person, virtual and hybrid events, including team meetings, training sessions, workshops, hackathons, global ESG programmes and all-company celebrations.
Handle event logistics, including room bookings, catering, A/V, signage, transport, parking and accessibility needs, and support day-of set-up, check-in, troubleshooting and breakdown.
Manage attendee communications: invitations, RSVPs, registration lists, reminders and post-event follow-up.
Build strong working relationships with building management, tenants and vendors, and maintain vendor lists, contracts and invoices.
Oversee swag and office and event inventory for new hires and upcoming events, including ordering, storage and distribution.
Support the Global Team Outing and other Workplace Experience projects alongside the wider team.
Who we look for
Experience in a People or HR operations, coordination or advisory role, ideally in a fast-growing tech or SaaS business.
Confidence handling first-line employee relations cases, with a working knowledge of UK employment law. Exposure to other European jurisdictions is a plus.
Hands-on experience with an HRIS and a case management system, inputting data, maintaining records and pulling reports you can trust.
Excellent organisation and attention to detail. You juggle competing priorities and deadlines without dropping the ball.
A real people person: a great listener and structured communicator who can deliver a “yes” and a “no” almost equally well.
A hands-on, can-do mindset. You’re happy switching between an advisory conversation, a systems clean-up and setting up a room for an event.
Proactive ownership. You anticipate needs, communicate early and follow through reliably.
You stay calm under pressure, professional and friendly, and you understand the need for confidentiality in everything people-related.
Flexible and adaptable, willing to step outside your immediate scope to make a real impact.
Business proficiency in English; another European language is a plus.
Comfortable with collaboration tools (Slack, Zoom, Google Workspace) and the usual office technology.

This role is focused on Jeeves ’s growth programs and emerging revenue channels — including our partnerships channel and new market expansion initiatives — where we need rigorous, scalable analytics to match the pace of growth.
You’ll be responsible for the analytical layer that connects our sales activity to revenue outcomes: building the dashboards our leadership relies on, maintaining shared responsibility for the integrity of our performance data, and proactively surfacing the insights that shape how we operate. You’ll work closely with the Head of Revenue Operations and contribute meaningfully to planning and review cycles alongside GTM leadership.
The pace here is real. Priorities shift, timelines compress, and the ground moves under your feet — not occasionally, but constantly. We need someone who is energized by that, not worn down. You won’t wait for someone to tell you what to look at. You’ll already know.

GTM Analytics & Growth Program Insights
Build and maintain Tableau dashboards tracking performance across our partnerships channel and new growth initiatives — serving audiences from country leads to executive leadership.
Analyze conversion rates, pipeline health, ramp trends, and revenue attainment across programs and segments, surfacing patterns before they become decisions that have already been made.
Come with a point of view. When a program is underperforming or a trend shifts, bring an interpretation and a recommendation (not just a chart).
Support quarterly and annual GTM business reviews with structured analysis: cohort breakdowns, market-level benchmarks, and forward-looking indicators.
Revenue Planning & Target Analysis
Contribute to GTM capacity planning and quota-setting cycles — modeling scenarios, building attainment reports, and stress-testing assumptions before plans are finalized.
Maintain performance-against-target reporting for growth programs and emerging channels: track attainment, flag outliers early, and ensure data is always reconciled.
Support variable compensation analysis for relevant programs — running calculations, auditing for accuracy, and partnering with Finance to ensure payouts are correct and timely.
Build and maintain data structures that support reliable rolling forecasts for new and high-growth segments.
AI-Driven Operations & Scale
Use AI tools, including Claude and other frontier models, as active parts of your workflow: automating repetitive reporting tasks, accelerating data synthesis, and building scalable analytical programs that would otherwise require a much larger team.
Identify RevOps processes that can be operationalized or significantly improved through AI, and take ownership of building those solutions, not just flagging the opportunity.
Apply AI-assisted analysis to extract insights at scale from large, multi-source datasets: pipeline signals, rep activity, customer behavior, and market trends.
Help establish Jeeves ’s AI-first approach to RevOps as a model for how the broader GTM team operates.
Data Quality & Systems Integration
Share responsibility for data quality across our revenue stack (HubSpot CRM, Tableau, and financial systems), conducting audits for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
Connect disparate data sources (CRM, marketing automation, financial tools, and proprietary revenue data) so that reporting on growth programs is unified and trustworthy.
Document data models, metric definitions, and reporting logic so the team works from a shared understanding of what we’re measuring and why.
Stakeholder Partnership
Develop enough context on our GTM motion to contribute meaningfully in planning and pipeline review cycles alongside sales leadership, bringing data that drives decisions, not just awareness.
Serve as a reliable analytical resource to the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM leadership: scope requests clearly, pull the data, and return clear answers quickly.
Identify process gaps and proactively propose improvements to how we collect, manage, and act on GTM data (especially across new and growing channels).

Tableau mastery: able to write complex calculated fields, build multi-source dashboards, and design views for diverse audiences from reps to the C-suite.
Advanced Excel and Google Sheets: complex formulas, pivot tables, and financial modeling — you reach for the right tool for the job, not just the most impressive one.
Strong SQL skills: you can get to an answer independently without waiting for a data engineer to pull it for you.
Data integration experience: comfortable connecting CRM, marketing automation, and financial data into unified reporting environments.
Business metrics fluency: deep understanding of conversion rates, customer lifetime value (LTV), pipeline coverage, ramp curves, revenue attainment, and customer health.
Data modeling: able to design clean structures that support accurate forecasting, compensation analysis, and multi-region rollups.
AI Fluency (Required, Not Optional)
You actively use AI tools, Claude Copilot/Code, or equivalent, as part of your day-to-day workflow, not as a novelty.
You’ve used AI to automate reporting pipelines, accelerate analysis, or build operational programs that scale beyond what a single analyst could do manually.
You’re curious about where AI can go next in RevOps and you bring ideas, not just execution.

Hungry and driven: you want to build something generational, and you bring the energy and output to match. You hold yourself to a higher standard than anyone else will hold you to.
Thrives in high-velocity environments: you’re not just comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — you’re energized by them. You find a way through, not a reason to wait.
High agency: you don’t wait for a ticket. You’re already thinking about what the data might be missing or what question leadership will ask next week.

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

We're building Halter in Argentina/Uruguay from the ground up, while still deeply connected to our global offices and ways of working. Sales teams will be remote across both Argentina and Uruguay, and our other teams will be in the Buenos Aires office. And we’re a fast growing team.
You'll bring the vibes and be our boots on the ground for the day-to-day people operations that keep our Argentina and Uruguay teams running. Reporting to our Senior People & Performance Partner in Boulder, CO (US), you'll own the logistics, systems and cultural moments that hold a growing team together: IT and onboarding, the office, our local vehicle fleet, and the team moments people actually remember.
You won't be doing it alone. You'll partner closely with our People Operations & Programs team in New Zealand, fleet, people systems, compliance and health & safety, onboarding programs, and you'll be the local expert they depend on for anything Argentina/Uruguay.
We're creating this role because we're growing fast in a brand-new market, and this work can't wait. When a laptop doesn't get signed for or a vehicle handover slips, someone's first week is worse for it. You'll be the person who makes sure that doesn't happen.
This is a hands-on, varied role for someone early in their career or making a career pivot. We don't care whether you've done people operations before. We care that you excel at whatever you put your mind to, that might have looked like your studies, your sport, or something you built on your own time.

s.h: What Your Day Will Look Like
s.t:
You're in early because it's a new starter's first day. Their desk is ready, their laptop is provisioned, their merch is sorted. You want to be the one who meets them at the door.
It's 9:40 and a vehicle handover has gone sideways, the depot window moved. You drop what you're doing and sort it, because a Territory Manager without a truck can't work.
You're partnering with the Global Vehicle Fleet lead in New Zealand, working on building a more scalable process.
You overhear the customer team saying they haven't had a proper team moment in weeks. You make a note and do something about it on Friday.
Executives are flying in from Auckland and Boulder next month for a fortnight. You make the whole visit feel effortless.
You hit something nobody has written a process for. You solve it, then write the process, for Argentina first, then Uruguay.
You spend a day out on farm with a Territory Manager, because you can't support work you've never seen.
In short: operational people threads, fleet, office, and creating genuinely good experiences for our Argentina and Uruguay teams. You'll be the ask-me-anything for everyone here.

Someone who fills other people's cups. Introvert or extrovert genuinely doesn't matter to us — some of the best people on our team are each. What matters is that you give energy rather than take it, and that people want to follow you whatever your title says.
A mindset of unreasonable hospitality. You bring a customer-service instinct to how you treat colleagues.
Comfortable being uncomfortable. You'll do the job nobody wants to do because you can see it needs doing. High humility, no ego about the task.
Strong operationally, with proven ability to execute in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. Timing matters here — most of this work can't wait a week.
A systems thinker. You'll get fluent in our people systems fast and become the local expert others come to. You like building the process, not just working the queue.
High awareness and empathy. You read between the lines and put yourself in other people's shoes.
Excellent judgment and discretion. Thoughtful, high-integrity, trustworthy. People will tell you difficult things and you'll know what to do with them.
You don't need a People background. Our team has come from hospitality, retail, services, agency and design. Delivery and curiosity beat a linear HR CV.
You've grown wherever you've been — promoted, trusted with more, handed the hard thing. Or you've followed what you find genuinely interesting rather than climbing a ladder. Both are good signals to us.
Hungry and ambitious , with the horsepower to grow as the business does.
Fluent in Spanish and English. You'll be the bridge between the Argentine team and colleagues in New Zealand and the US.
Based in Buenos Aires and up for five days a week with the team. Our space is in Vicente López to start.
Genuinely interested in the work — land, livestock, and the people who farm it.
Where this could go
We're not hiring a coordinator forever. We're hiring the person who builds the foundation in Argentina, then helps us do it again in Uruguay and beyond. If you're good, this is one of the best seats in the company to grow from.
What this role isn't
Some of this work is physical, urgent and unglamorous. You'll sign for deliveries and stand in queues. Processes will break and you'll be the one who notices. There's no playbook yet, and for a while you'll be writing it while doing the job. If that sounds frustrating rather than exciting, this isn't the right role — and that's genuinely fine.
Our Office First Approach
Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.
We're office first, not office only. Working from the office is our default, but we flex when needed. We have a high-trust culture where everyone is trusted to do what's best for Halter.
Our office vibe is special, the high energy and spectacular people make work enjoyable. Your growth and impact are unlimited here, coming from solving problems, innovating, and constantly learning from each other.
Join our team
Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement.

If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

🎤 Why voize? Because we're more than just a job!
At voize, we believe the greatest gift to frontline workers is time - time to care, connect, and be present. Today, that time is lost to busywork and complex systems that pull them away from what matters most: people .
Our vision is to change that by building AI companions that seamlessly take over digital workflows. We don't replace humans with technology - we amplify their impact.
Our mission is backed with a $50M Series A funding led by Balderton Capital , with support from HV Capital, Y Combinator and other leading VCs. Today, 2,000+ facilities trust voize, and over 200,000 users rely on our AI companion to ease their daily workload.
As a dynamic team, we combine first-in-class technology with meaningful social impact. And now, we're looking for you to join us on this mission!

s.h: 💡 Your Mission: Turn growth into a system!
s.t:
Hi, I'm Jeremy, I lead RevOps at voize. I'm hiring the person who owns sales operations as we scale: new markets, new segments, and a sales team growing fast in all of them.
As Sales Operations Manager, you build the GTM engine that carries us past €100M ARR, working in close partnership with our sales leaders, with genuinely good tooling and AI ways of working behind you. Joining at this point in our hyper-growth journey is rare: big enough that the problems are real, early enough that you shape how they get solved. What you build now compounds for years, and so does your scope.
This role is roughly 60% building new process and 40% running what exists. If you want a mature machine to optimize, this is not it. If you want to design the machine, for now and for what comes next, it is.
🚀 Your Daily Business - No two days are alike
Territory, compensation & capacity. Own the global account, territory and book-of-business model. Carve books for new AEs, keep segmentation honest as we add hospitals and new geos, and build the capacity and quota model that underpins our fiscal plan.
Forecasting. Run the forecast process end to end with our VP Sales and team leads: weekly hygiene, submit and roll-up, quarterly commit. Diagnose why deals slip, and stand the process up in the US, France and UK as those teams ramp.
Insights the company acts on. Define the sales metrics we run on, then turn pipeline and funnel data into the analysis that steers board meetings, monthly GTM reviews and weekly deal inspection. You define what gets measured; our data and BI team build the layer underneath.
Commercial process. Design how non-standard deals are managed at voize. You set the rules and stand the function up; you will not be the approval queue.
Process and tool enablement. In close collaboration with sales enablement, you make sure what gets built actually gets adopted, partnering with leaders, AEs and SDRs to prioritize the work with the most impact.
The GTM stack, built AI-first. Own the sales side of CRM and the tools around it. Automate the manual layer with Claude, n8n and whatever else earns its place, and take a real position on which tooling we buy next as we scale.

s.h: 🤝 Your Skillset - What you bring to the table
s.t:
3+ years in revenue operations, sales operations or GTM strategy , at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company or in strategy/tech consulting, VC or M&A before an operating role. You have seen what breaks as a sales team scales, because you were the one who fixed it.
Exceptional stakeholder skills. You partner with VPs and team leads as an equal, push back with evidence, and get change adopted by people who do not report to you.
Sharp analytical instincts and deep CRM fluency. Expert in spreadsheets, comfortable reading data in a BI tool, and you have owned a HubSpot or Salesforce instance rather than just worked in one. You go deep on data enrichment and spot the patterns that keep our data model trustworthy.
You have supported forecasting. You can talk methodology, where it broke, and what you changed. Same for a territory or quota plan you built and aligned with sales leadership.
Entrepreneurial mindset and hands-on. You are comfortable with no playbook, you prioritize ruthlessly, and you ship rather than produce recommendations.
AI-native as a builder, not just a user. You already use Claude, n8n or similar to remove manual work from your own day, and you can point to something concrete you shipped that way.
🌱 Growing together - what you can expect at voize
We are a fast-growing startup, that means you will take on real problems, grow quickly, and make a real impact, giving frontline workers more time for people
We foster an open, collaborative culture with regular team events, whether you work from our Berlin office or remotely across Germany
Become a co-creator of our success with stock options
Generous perks: 30 vacation days plus your birthday off, Germany Transport Ticket, Urban Sports Club, regular company off-sites, and access to learning platforms such as Blinkist and Audible, plus free language courses
You decide when you work best, that means flexible working hours and a good hybrid set-up.

We look forward to your application and can't wait to meet you - no matter who you are or what background you have!

Partner Operations Manager
The Global Merchant Excellence team
The Merchant excellence team supports accountable for supporting restaurant and retail partners across all markets with key onboarding and lifecycle tasks, acting as their operational support team once they’re live on the platform.

Manages partner contacts across live and non‑live channels globally, with UKIE representing the largest share of demand.
Handles admin and technical tasks for SMB, Mid‑Market and National partners (e.g. account and menu creation, menu edits, tablet installation and troubleshooting, photography, compliance actions like DAC7, refund disputes, and inbound phone/chat support).
Acts as the sole point of contact for self‑serve partners after they “graduate” from early‑life onboarding, working closely with New Partner Experience and Account Management teams.
Operationally, most day‑to‑day volume is handled by third‑party vendors aligned by language and market, with in‑house L2 teams owning complex queries, escalations, and performance management across markets.

s.h: In this role you'll be involved in these key areas
s.t:
Managing channel, queue and team leader/ agent performance across our in-house teams in Manchester, UK and Milan, Italy.
Identifying trends in performance and conducting root cause analysis (e.g. Team Leader/agent productivity) to drive improved performance.
Helping define new metrics, targets and best practices to drive improvements in Merchant experience (e.g. first touch resolution)
Present market performance updates and strategic implications to executive leadership.
Identify Operational efficiencies that can be gained through automation and process improvements.
What you’ll be doing
Monitoring and Tracking: Daily/weekly monitoring of key performance indicators (KPIs) for channels (e.g., chat, email, phone), service queues, team leaders, and individual agents across UKI and EU.
Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Conducting deep dives and methodical investigations to identify the fundamental reasons behind performance trends (e.g., analysing agent productivity, training gaps, system errors, or vendor operational issues).
Trend Identification: Analysing data to spot emerging or recurring patterns in team and channel performance, service demand, and partner feedback.
Developing and delivering clear, data-driven presentations on current market performance (likely related to partner satisfaction or service delivery) and the strategic impact of those results to executive leadership.
Insight Generation: Translating raw performance data and market trends into actionable insights and strategic recommendations for senior decision-makers.
New Metric Development: Collaborating with stakeholders to research, define, pilot, and implement new service metrics (e.g., specific definitions for "First Touch Resolution" or “Merchant Effort Score") that better reflect merchant experience and business objectives.
Target Setting: Establishing challenging yet realistic performance targets and benchmarks for teams based on data analysis and industry best practices.
Best Practice Documentation: Documenting and disseminating successful processes, operational standards, and agent/team leader best practices across the UKI and EU servicing in-house teams..
Opportunity Identification: Auditing existing workflows and processes to pinpoint areas where operational efficiencies can be achieved (e.g., manual data entry, handoffs between teams).
Automation Scoping: Proposing and evaluating potential automation solutions (e.g., RPA, self-service tools, AI-assisted routing) to reduce manual effort and improve service speed.
Implementation Support: Collaborating with technology and operations teams to pilot, test, and roll out approved process improvements and automation initiatives.
All these activities may extend to other LOBs as well as Partner Operations.

Is comfortable leading updates and can speak up when working with more senior stakeholders and partners
Is knowledgeable of CRM systems (e.g. Zendesk / Salesforce) and has experience of creating reports across systems

The best of your adventures is the one you have yet to sail!
## Your Purpose ##
Here at MSC Cruises we are looking for a Public Health Operations Manager to drive and oversee the public health operations in Brazil for MSC Cruises and Explora Journeys, acting as the key strategic partner to Brazil-s National Health Surveillance Agency (ANVISA) and other government health authorities.
You will champion regulatory excellence by ensuring full compliance with national public health requirements while enabling safe, efficient, and uninterrupted vessel operations.

The Public Health Operations Manager will also lead the design and delivery of impactful seasonal training programs, strengthen high-value relationships across local and federal health networks, and proactively influence public health initiatives that support operational success, exceptional guest experiences, and the continued growth of the business in the Brazilian market.

Public Health Operations & Compliance
* Ensure full compliance with Brazilian public health regulations across all relevant operations, including vessels calling at Brazilian ports.
* Monitor and ensure compliance with sanitation, epidemiological surveillance, potable water safety, food safety, pest control, and waste management standards.
* Coordinate inspections and audits with ANVISA and other Brazilian health authorities.
* Maintain and verify documentation required for vessel entry into Brazilian ports
Policy Monitoring, Development & Strategic Planning
* Stay up to date with changes in ANVISA regulations, policies, and inspection protocols.
* Communicate updates to relevant stakeholders and ensure operational alignment.
* Draft and update public health policies and SOPs for Brazilian operations, incorporating ANVISA requirements aligned with ANVISA-s Guide nº 65/2023 and other relevant legislation, in addition to international best practices (e.g., CDC VSP, SHIPSAN).
* Update outbreak response plans as needed for MSC / Explora Journeys and coordinate with onboard medical teams during public health events.
Liaison & Stakeholder Engagement
* Serve as the primary contact for ANVISA for both cruise brands, facilitating communication, inspections, and reporting.
* Represent Explora Journeys and MSC Cruises in regulatory meetings, industry forums, and collaborative initiatives with Brazilian health authorities.
* Build strong relationships with port health officials, local service providers, and internal stakeholders.
Training & Capacity Building
* Provide training and guidance to shipboard and shoreside teams on Brazilian public health standards.
* Support onboarding and continuous education for Public Health Officers and medical staff operating in Brazilian waters.
* Guide and support vessels in preparing for ANVISA inspections, including documentation, procedural readiness, and crew awareness.
Response Management
* Prepare and deliver timely, accurate responses to ANVISA queries and communications.
* Collaborate closely with the UK Public Health Team and MSC Brazil Legal Team to ensure responses are aligned, well-supported, and strategically delivered.
* Review and challenge ANVISA infraction notices where appropriate, ensuring a coordinated and evidence-based approach.
Internal Audit Programme
* Collaborate with MSCCM Public Health and Food Safety stakeholders to develop and implement an internal audit program aligned with ANVISA standards to proactively identify and address compliance gaps.
## Your Journey so far ##
* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Public Health or a related field.
* Proven track record in regulatory affairs, public health compliance, or maritime health operations.
* Professional experience working within or in close collaboration with ANVISA is strongly preferred.
* Deep understanding of ANVISA regulations and inspection procedures.
* Familiarity with international public health standards (USPH, SHIPSAN, ANVISA, WHO).
* Experience in outbreak investigation and response planning.
* In-depth knowledge of ANVISA regulations and Brazilian health legislation.
* Experience liaising with government agencies and drafting regulatory policy.
* Strong analytical, communication, negotiation and leadership skills.
* Ability to work cross-functionally with international teams.
* Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and other web-based collaboration tools (e.g., SharePoint, Teams).
* Fluent in Portuguese & English (written and spoken).
## Your Essentials ##
* Translating technical information into accessible language.
* Strong written and verbal communication.
* Long-term vision for public health policies and operations.
* Data-driven and impact-oriented decision-making.
* Prioritization in complex environments.
## Our commitment ##
We are committed to building a future that values diverse perspectives, embraces the world beyond borders, and fosters an inclusive environment where every individual feels valued, respected and empowered to be their authentic selves. Our commitment extends to taking meaningful, measurable actions that have a long-term positive impact on our guests, our employees and our planet.
Ready to turn your passion into something extraordinary? Join us at MSC Cruises, where new opportunities await. Apply today to be part of a global team that is pushing boundaries and achieving something remarkable. Your journey starts here!

Initiative-driven with a strong problem-solving mindset and the ability to adapt to changing situations and requirements.

You'll take on ambiguous, high impact questions and turn them into clearly defined problems, design the right solution, and drive it through build, adoption, and continuous improvement.
The role has three modes. First, you'll drive the analytical core: forecasting, executive reporting, revenue planning, QBR-grade analyses over large datasets, quota and target analytics, and the models that support forecasting and planning. Second, you'll build net-new systems: internal tools, data models, and reporting infrastructure that teammates then run and scale. That includes planning models, dashboards, and operational workflows that make the business more efficient over time.
Third, you'll make Revenue Operations more leveraged with AI, whether that's building AI-assisted tooling, designing account scoring and research logic in our go-to-market stack, or automating work that shouldn't be manual. You’ll constantly look for more opportunities to increase leverage across the organization.
The ideal candidate combines strong analytical horsepower with a systems mindset and genuine comfort with ambiguity. You ask why until you understand the business objective behind a request, you design solutions that scale beyond the first use case, and you already use AI to build and move faster than your job title suggests.

You’re naturally curious about how AI can improve the way work gets done, but you know technology is only valuable when it solves a real business problem. And you finish: to you, work is done when it's adopted, documented, and running without you, not when the analysis is shipped.
This role is based out of our NYC office.

If you want your creativity to drive growth and shape perception, this is the place.

The Brex Marketing team is looking for an experienced Senior Marketing Operations Manager to architect and optimize our B2B sales-led and channel-driven GTM engine. This role will define and maintain the systems, processes, and operational rigor that align Marketing, SDR, Sales, and Partner teams.
We are looking for someone who is eager to design the future-state GTM tech stack—modernizing how leads flow, how insights are generated, and how operational workloads become more efficient through automation, AI, and agentic workflows. This person will champion operational excellence by improving lead management, automating revenue processes, increasing funnel velocity, and enabling more efficient cross-functional alignment.
Where you’ll work
This role will be based in our Vancouver office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Own and evolve the GTM systems architecture, ensuring Salesforce, Marketo, LeanData, ZoomInfo, Qualified, Outreach, and Clay.io work together as a best-in-class, integrated ecosystem.
Lead the design, governance, and optimization of data orchestration workflows using LeanData, including routing, prioritization, handoffs, and conversion logic across Marketing, SDR, and Sales teams.
Design and execute a future-state operational roadmap focused on scaling B2B demand generation, ABM, and partner-led growth through automation, improved data flows, and AI-powered insights.
Build automated lifecycle processes for lead scoring, enrichment, qualification, and cross-functional handoffs using LeanData, Zapier, Clay, Segment, and AI agents.
Enhance sales productivity by implementing agentic workflows (e.g., automated follow-ups, enrichment workflows, SDR assistance tools) in Outreach and Salesforce.
Manage data governance across Salesforce, Marketo, and Segment, ensuring reliable attribution, reporting, and pipeline visibility.
Create AI-informed dashboards and reporting on pipeline performance, lead velocity, conversion, campaign effectiveness, and partner impact.
Partner with RevOps, Sales Systems, and Engineering to operationalize cross-functional processes that reduce manual work and improve efficiency.
Support partner/VAR motions through automated attribution, routing rules, partner engagement workflows, and integrated co-marketing processes.
Continuously evaluate new tools, AI capabilities, and operational improvements that elevate our GTM infrastructure.

4+ years in Marketing Operations or Revenue Operations supporting B2B sales-led funnels.
Hands-on experience administering Marketo, Salesforce, and LeanData.
Deep expertise with lead routing, lead-to-account matching, and data orchestration workflows using LeanData or similar workflow automation tools.
Proven ability to design automated workflows, operational processes, and scalable cross-system integrations.
Experience using AI-driven tools or agentic workflows to automate SDR tasks, enrich lead data, or accelerate GTM execution.
Strong analytical, system design, and documentation skills; able to translate business needs into scalable technical workflows.
Experience collaborating with Sales, SDR, RevOps, and System/Engineering teams.

Experience in FinTech or enterprise B2B SaaS environments.
Familiarity with conversational marketing/ABM platforms like Qualified.
Experience with tools like LeanData and Outreach in support of lead routing and SDR/BDR workflows.
Experience with paid funnel operations is a plus (Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, etc.).
Understanding of partner/VAR operational workflows and partner attribution logic.
Ability to design scalable integrations using tools like Segment, Zapier, or Workato-style platforms.

Taskrabbit is a marketplace platform that conveniently connects people with Taskers to handle everyday home to-do’s, such as furniture assembly, handyman work, moving help, and much more.
At Taskrabbit, we want to transform lives one task at a time. As a company we celebrate innovation, inclusion and hard work. Our culture is collaborative, pragmatic, and fast-paced. We’re looking for talented, entrepreneurially minded and data-driven people who also have a passion for helping people do what they love.

Together with IKEA, we’re creating more opportunities for people to earn a consistent, meaningful income on their own terms by building lasting relationships with clients in communities around the world.
Taskrabbit is a hybrid company with employees distributed across the US and EU and a Built In — Best Places to Work (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) continually ranked across multiple national and regional categories. Join us at Taskrabbit, where your work will be meaningful, your ideas valued, and your potential unleashed!
This role operates on a hybrid schedule requiring two days of in-office collaboration per week. The position must be based out of our New York City office.

Taskrabbit connects busy people in need of help with trusted local Taskers who can lend a hand with everything from home repairs to errands, with the goal of being the number one home services platform in the countries we serve. A Tasker gets paid to do what they love, when and where they want — all while saving the day for someone in their city.

The Tasker Operations team helps Taskers achieve their personal tasking goals using Taskrabbit. The Tasker Operations Manager plays a critical role in onboarding Taskers seamlessly, nurturing them, ensuring that they are fully utilized and retained, and building satisfaction with the platform.

We’re proactive—helping Taskers before they realize they need support. These approaches, employed at the local level, result in higher quality, more retentive, and more satisfied Taskers.

The work you do will support our overall managed marketplace strategy, helping to ensure that every job gets done so well that Taskers and clients come back again and again.
You will be responsible for a specific set of metropolitan areas, driving key metrics for the company as well as supply alignment in those metros, which result in increased invoices and revenue. You will be the face of Taskrabbit to Taskers in your market and seen as a regional expert across the organization.

Drive invoices and revenue by analyzing supply data and taking targeted action to improve supply health, booking conversion, and Tasker quality across the Tasker lifecycle (activation, billing, retention, churn) — advising or acting directly to acquire quality Taskers when needed.
Act as a regional subject-matter expert, monitoring market performance and tailoring programs and supply tactics to local dynamics.
Coach Taskers in your Book of Business (primarily in group settings, in-person and virtual) and grow participation in scaled lifecycle programs, choosing the right channels to reach them.
Master the Tasker lifecycle, using data-driven insights and strong data fluency to identify gaps, design and lead experiments, and communicate performance insights and business impact to teams and leadership.
Be a product expert — know what's live, explain it to Taskers, and validate/submit bug reports based on Tasker feedback.
Lead community engagement (office hours, profile workshops, socials) and work cross-functionally with Product, Support, Partnerships, Marketing, Legal, and Commercial Ops to advocate for Tasker solutions that drive invoices and revenue.
Share learnings, pitfalls, and wins with the global Tasker Operations team; travel up to 10% for metro events.

Full professional fluency in English and Russian .
Based in New York City or an easily commutable distance, with availability to travel to other regions as required.
3+ years in marketplace operations, customer success, community management, or comparable roles; Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
A proficient user of data to derive actionable insights and make decisions; proficient with BI, Google Workspace, and customer success tools. (SQL & Sigma experience preferred)
A highly effective, confident communicator who can engage audiences from 1 to 100.
A low-ego, opportunistic self-starter who's comfortable problem-solving on the fly in a fast-paced, globally distributed team, and knows when to ask for help.
An enthusiastic people person with strong cross-functional relationship-building skills, excellent organization and attention to detail, and a genuine passion and playfulness for the work.

At Taskrabbit, our approach to compensation is designed to be competitive, transparent, and equitable. Total compensation consists of base pay + bonus + benefits + perks.
The base pay range for this position is $72,000 - $97,000. This range is representative of base pay only, and does not include any other total cash compensation amounts, such as company bonus or benefits. Final offer amounts may vary from the amounts listed above and will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, qualifications, geography, and level.

Taskrabbit is a Hybrid Company. We value flexibility and choice but also stay committed to regular in-person connection.
The People. You will be surrounded by some of the most talented, supportive, smart, and kind leaders and teams -- people you can be proud to work with!
The Diverse Culture. We believe that we make better decisions when our workforce reflects the diversity of the communities in which we operate. Women make up half of our leadership team and our diversity representation is above that of the tech industry average.
The Perks. Taskrabbit offers our employees with employer-paid health insurance and a 401k match with immediate vesting for our US based employees. We offer all of our global employees generous and flexible time off with 2 company-wide closure weeks, Taskrabbit product stipends, wellness + productivity + education stipends, IKEA discounts, reproductive health support, and more. Benefits vary by country of employment.
