As a Program Specialist (Operations Manager), you will perform the following duties at the full performance GS-13 grade level: Contribute to establishing the Department's strategic direction by identifying and advancing key goals, objectives, and initiatives.

Support the development and implementation of Department-wide policies, procedures, and operational standards to promote consistency, effectiveness, and alignment with organizational priorities. Lead and support special projects and serve on multidisciplinary teams to address operational priorities, emerging issues, and Departmental initiatives.

Promote a culture of safety by ensuring patient and staff safety standards, policies, and requirements are effectively implemented and consistently followed.

Assess staff and organizational performance in achieving established goals and objectives, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, effectiveness, quality, and compliance with Clinical Center policies and regulatory requirements. Implement budget strategies that align resources with Departmental priorities and organizational objectives.

Prepare reports, analyses, and recommendations to inform decision-making at the Department, Clinical Center, and NIH levels. Monitor the delivery of high-quality customer service to DPM patients receiving anesthesia and operative care, ensuring the timeliness, quality, and scope of services effectively meet patient and operational needs.

Evaluate and respond to complaints, suggestions, and requests regarding perioperative services, elevating if necessary. Ensure staff are appropriately trained in the use of equipment, technology, and information systems that support Departmental workflows and anesthesia care, including operating room video and imaging systems.

Serve as a member of the Department's management team, collaborating with senior medical, nursing, administrative, and other key staff to advance Departmental priorities and operations.

Coordinate with stakeholders regarding operating room integration systems (e.g., StreamConnect, POIS) and operating room imaging software, communicating system updates and changes in policies or protocols to DPM and OR Nursing staff, gathering user feedback, and facilitating the resolution of technology-related issues.

Consult with the Chief of the Department on the maintenance, servicing, and operational readiness of DPM equipment. Collaborate with vendors and evaluate new equipment, technologies, and software to assess their potential impact on clinical care, research protocols, emerging techniques, and organizational performance.

Develop recommendations regarding acquisitions that support the needs and priorities of the Department and Clinical Center.

If selected at the GS-11 or GS-12 grade level, you will essentially perform the same duties as those described above; however, duties will be less complex and will be performed under closer supervision with more detailed guidance.
In order to qualify for a Program Specialist (Operations Manager) at the GS-11 grade level, you must have: A. completed a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or an LL.M., if related; OR B. 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks: 1) Supporting program management activities involving patient safety and customer service; 2) Supporting the development of procurement packages for specialty medical equipment and supplies; 3) Supporting the lifecycle management of specialty medical equipment and technologies; 4) Participating in administrative operational activities by preparing reports and analyses; 5) Coordinating with physicians and other medical staff to support operating room workflow.

OR C. a combination of post baccalaureate education related to the position and experience that meets 100% of the qualification requirements for this position.

In order to qualify for a Program Specialist (Operations Manager) at the GS-12 grade level, you must have 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-11 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks: 1) Performing program management of perioperative operations to meet strategic operational objectives; 2) Overseeing the development of procurement packages for operating room equipment and supplies; 3) Managing operating room technologies, including maintenance, updates, interoperability, and user support; 4) Evaluating and providing recommendations for patient safety compliance and service quality; 5) Collaborating with multidisciplinary stakeholders to enhance outcomes for clinical research activities.

In order to qualify for a Program Specialist (Operations Manager) at the GS-13 grade level, you must have 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks: 1) Leading the strategic management of perioperative operations that affect patient care and clinical research (i.e., organizational priorities, policies, operational standards, performance expectations, and improvement initiatives); 2) Overseeing the lifecyle process of acquisitions involving operating room technologies; 3) Serving as the technical authority for advanced operating room systems and equipment (i.e., endoscopy systems, Provation or comparable clinical software, surgical robotics, computerized microscopes, electrosurgical equipment, operating room tables, and OR integration systems (e.g., Stream Connect or POIS)); 4) Providing senior-level oversight of perioperative operations.

(i.e., resource utilization, organizational performance, workforce readiness, patient safety, service quality, and appropriate lifecycle management of clinical equipment and technology); 5) Negotiating with and disseminating information to multidisciplinary stakeholders to enhance outcomes for perioperative research activities.

You will receive credit for all experience material to the position, including experience gained in religious, civic, welfare, service, and organizational activities, regardless of whether you received pay.

About 9fin
9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion.
Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets.
Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption.
We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide.
The opportunity
We're hiring our first dedicated legal operations team member to sit at the heart of 9fin's growing Legal Affairs function. This is a broad, hands-on role and a rare opportunity to shape how a scale-up in-house legal team runs from the inside out.
You'll own the operational engine of the team: our contract lifecycle platform (Ironclad, which is deeply embedded across sales, procurement and RevOps), our commercial playbook (and developing non-commercial playbooks), our tech stack (including AI implementation), our front-door (right now, ticketing is done in Linear), our knowledge management (currently spread across multiple systems), our reporting and KPIs, and the tracking and governance around outside counsel spend.
You'll also be a project manager and a hands-on partner to the General Counsel. That includes co-drafting monthly and quarterly business reviews, leading and coordinating cross-functional initiatives (for example M&A diligence coordination, trademark portfolio work, or regulatory readiness workstreams), and holding a high bar for organisation so nothing on a small, fast-moving team drops.
You'll report to the General Counsel and work alongside legal colleagues in London and New York. This is a London-based role and we typically expect the team to be in the office three days a week.
What you’ll work on
Below is the shape of the role, laid out as prioritised by Now, Next and Later so you can see the broad strokes of the path ahead - but by no means is this set in stone. Priorities will move as we learn what's most useful in practice and you’ll have a big hand in shaping this further.
Now
Tune legal intake - help us build out the “front door” for legal requests across the business.
Partner with Sales, Finance, InfoSec and Procurement to streamline deal-desk and approval processes
Support on knowledge management and internal policy administration. Consolidate knowledge, templates, and other information in a clean accessible structure.
Build our external legal spend tracker from scratch. Categorise spend, log invoices and quotes, match to matter, and produce a monthly view for the General Counsel.
Own KPI reporting improvements against our Ironclad-fed dashboards. Expand coverage into intake, spend, cycle times, and other operational metrics.
Own operational and reporting support across the Legal function, including responses to internal stakeholders including Finance, RevOps, and the People team.
Next
Get inside and own our tech stack and know it end-to-end - Ironclad, Linear, Google Workspace, Notion, and the AI tools we've adopted or are evaluating.
Build, maintain and roll out templates, playbooks and self-serve legal resources so the business can move quickly.
Own Ironclad workflow hygiene and adoption end-to-end. Work with the team to clean up metadata and archiving, tighten approvals and signatory workflows, and work with commercial counsel to roll out training across sales, procurement, RevOps and other frequent users.
Bring structure and visibility across the team. Keep track of open projects, drive follow-through, and make sure balls do not drop across a small team with a lot of surface area.
Maintain our sales contract playbook. Keep it current, propose updates as commercial patterns and RevOps feedback surface them, and make sure the team is actually using it.
Later
Partner with the General Counsel to produce meaningful Exec-level reporting.
Assist with management of large legal projects on GC instruction. Recent examples include M&A diligence coordination, and trademark portfolio work.
Support company secretarial administration.

We're looking for a highly organised operator who is energised by building order out of scale-up complexity. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you do need to have run legal operations end-to-end before. The essentials come first below, followed by preferred experience and the traits we care about most.
Highly organised with a systems mindset: You keep the plates spinning and notice when one wobbles. You see the workflow behind the task and design for repeatability.
Commercial, action-biased, comfortable with ambiguity: You understand what the business needs from legal, get things over the line without waiting to be asked twice, and you're comfortable being the first hire writing the map as you go.
Ironclad or equivalent CLM: Hands-on experience with Ironclad or a directly comparable enterprise CLM (for example Juro, LinkSquares, Icertis, Agiloft, Leah). We are deeply embedded in Ironclad and you will own it.
Legal operations track record: At least five years' experience running legal operations, contracts operations or a closely adjacent function (compliance operations, legal project management, or legal chief-of-staff), ideally in a scale-up or in-house legal team that is fast paced and where you can demonstrate ownership.
End-to-end project delivery: You have owned legal or cross-functional projects on your own steam, including timelines, risks, stakeholders and outcomes.
Reporting and data fluency: You can build clean dashboards, work with a KPI framework, and translate metrics into a story someone can act on.
Outside counsel spend or panel exposure: Experience setting up spend tracking, panel management or legal project management would be useful, but we're also open to someone with the capability and appetite to build this from scratch.
Builder mentality: Experience as a team’s first or only legal-ops hire, or a member of a small team in the early stage of the build-out of a legal ops function, would be a strong advantage.

We’re a scaling start up, and we enjoy sharing our success, when the company succeeds, we always reinvest that in our people. We also offer huge amounts of responsibility, an abundance of opportunity for growth and a platform to truly excel.

Exceptional Attention to Detail: This is the #1 quality we are hiring for. You naturally catch the typo, the wrong date, or the skipped step. You verify everything before you submit and hold yourself to a standard that goes far beyond "good enough."

The Campaign Operations Coordinator plays an essential role in the successful execution of influencer marketing campaigns at NeoReach . This position ensures that campaigns run smoothly from kickoff to completion, with a focus on organization, communication, and delivering measurable results for our clients.

Acting as the bridge between internal teams, influencers, and brand partners, the Campaign Operations Coordinator is responsible for managing timelines, coordinating deliverables, reviewing content, and tracking performance metrics.

This role requires exceptional attention to detail, a proactive approach to problem-solving, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.
Campaign Execution & Coordination
Oversee and manage the day-to-day operations of influencer marketing campaigns, ensuring timely execution and delivery of all campaign deliverables.
Coordinate with internal teams (creative, paid media, account management, etc.) to ensure all deliverables align with the client’s strategy and objectives.
Serve as the main point of contact for influencers, ensuring clear communication on campaign objectives, content expectations, timelines, and brand guidelines.
Influencer Identification & Outreach
Research and select influencers that align with client goals, campaign strategy, and target audience demographics.
Conduct outreach, manage negotiations, and finalize influencer contracts in coordination with the Account Director.
Ensure influencers receive all necessary campaign materials, including creative briefs and brand guidelines, to execute content effectively.
Content Review & Approvals
Review influencer content to ensure it meets brand messaging, tone, and campaign objectives.
Collaborate with Account Directors and clients to approve content before publication.
Provide feedback and revisions to influencers to ensure all deliverables meet brand compliance standards.
Tracking & Reporting
Monitor campaign performance metrics (reach, impressions, engagement, conversions, etc.) throughout the campaign lifecycle.
Compile and deliver regular campaign performance reports to Account Directors, including KPI tracking, insights, and recommendations for optimization.
Maintain detailed records of campaign deliverables, approvals, and timelines to keep campaigns on schedule.
Relationship Management
Build and maintain strong relationships with influencers and creators to foster long-term collaboration opportunities.
Act as the liaison between clients, influencers, and internal teams to ensure alignment and transparent communication.
Troubleshoot and resolve issues quickly to minimize disruptions to campaign flow.
Post-Campaign Analysis
Partner with Account Directors to evaluate campaign success, ROI, and strategic takeaways.
Consolidate learnings and provide actionable recommendations for future campaigns.
Issue Resolution & Problem Solving
Work closely with Account Directors to address any challenges related to influencer performance, content quality, or platform issues.
Identify and implement solutions promptly to keep campaigns on track.

1–3 years of experience in influencer marketing, campaign coordination, account management, or a related field.
Proven ability to manage multiple campaigns and deadlines simultaneously.
Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for both internal and external correspondence.
Experience working with influencer management platforms, project management tools, and analytics dashboards is preferred.
Ability to analyze performance data and translate it into actionable recommendations.
Proactive problem-solver with a collaborative mindset.
Passion for influencer marketing, digital media, and emerging social platforms.

Experience working with influencers across multiple platforms (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, etc.).
Proficiency in using influencer marketing tools and campaign management software.
Familiarity with paid media strategies to amplify influencer content.

This role offers a competitive base salary, complemented by a performance-driven commission structure.

Funnel Leasing Inc., is hiring for a Strategy & Operations Manager, AI. The Strategy & Operations Manager, AI is responsible for driving the strategic direction and go-to-market strategy for Funnel’s cutting-edge AI products, becoming the accountable party for the segment’s P&L.

Collaborating closely with customers of all sizes, you'll gain valuable insights into their AI strategies, ensuring seamless alignment of Funnel’s products with their unique needs and Funnel’s overarching goals.

Your role will involve conducting research to pinpoint trends, customer preferences, and competitive dynamics that will inform Funnel’s corporate strategy and product roadmap. With ownership of Funnel’s pricing and packaging strategies, you'll strike the balance between product value, market demand, and profit margin.

You will have the responsibility of leading and elevating the future of Funnel’s AI-driven solutions while improving the country’s rental experience. The Salary range for this role is $125,000 to $145,000/year.
Why Funnel?
We are a 'work from anywhere' in the U.S. SaaS company that centers our services on the renter experience. We develop amazing software that has revolutionized the #proptech industry. And did we mention we have an amazing team that is on #FunnelFire!? Oh, did we forget to tell you we have unlimited PTO, benefits that begin on your first day of employment, P.I.N.K. core values that ROCK, and our team puts the FUN in Funnel!
Who is Funnel Leasing ?
Have you ever rented an apartment and wished the process could be better? At Funnel we do too. We know we need to make the process of renting an apartment as easy as purchasing socks on Amazon. We’ve created cloud-based marketing and leasing software that delivers the ultimate rental experience for everyone involved in the process. We’re in the process of transforming the real estate industry through cutting-edge technology built, sold, and supported by the most passionate people you’ll meet.
The Strategy & Operations Manager, AI essential roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

Lead the strategy and GTM approach for Funnel’s AI products (VLA, VVLA, MA, & new AI offerings/integrations).
Track and analyze financial data to make informed decisions regarding resource allocation, investment opportunities, and cost optimization, being accountable for the financial success of Funnel’s AI segment P&L (Will work with Finance to create a P&L).
Take ownership of pricing and packaging strategies in collaboration with sales/marketing, optimizing them to reflect product value and market demands, with the goal of maximizing margins where possible.
Conduct market research to identify trends, customer preferences, and competitive dynamics which you will use to inform Funnel’s product and strategy decisions.
Collaborate with customers of all sizes (e.g., Enterprise, Mid-Market) to gain insights into their AI strategies; ensuring that our products are aligned with their needs / objectives.
Drive the evaluation between off-the-shelf and proprietary AI solutions, considering the dynamic landscape of the industry.
Be the connective tissue between product/engineering, revenue, and CX regarding Funnel’s AI related products and strategy.
Strategically engage in select sales engagements to accelerate segment attachment, overall ARR growth, and increase the percentage of Funnel ARR from the segment.
Manage various product marketing initiatives around Funnel’s suite of AI products, ensuring Funnel is successfully selling the value of the products (throughout marketing/sales lifecycle) and bringing new AI products to market.
Engage with executive leadership, department heads, and external stakeholders to harmonize product strategies with overarching organizational goals.
Travel: < 5%

Seu bem-estar, nossa missão. Junte-se a uma empresa que torna o mundo mais saudável.

Essa é uma vaga afirmativa para Pessoas com Deficiência.

Para alcançar a nossa missão, é essencial que existam diversas perspectivas aqui dentro e que todas as pessoas se sintam acolhidas, valorizadas e empoderadas no Wellhub.

Estamos contratando Business Operations Analyst para se juntar ao nosso time de Business Transformation em São Paulo!
Nossa missão é aprimorar a rotina operacional de nossas pessoas clientes, tornando nossos processos escaláveis e padronizados, buscando ser a área de referência dentro do Wellhub e garantindo a qualidade na execução, sempre em parceria com outros times internos.
O objetivo do time de Client Operations LatAm é garantir a eficiência, a qualidade e a execução correta dos processos dos clientes de RH, em alinhamento com os times de vendas e finanças.
Como parte do time, você atuará em contato com nossas pessoas clientes externas, prestando suporte na análise de dados, apoiando os times de vendas nos processos estabelecidos e trabalhando para assegurar o cumprimento dos alinhamentos operacionais.

Identificar e mapear oportunidades de melhoria para o time de Operações e para o pilar de clientes como um todo.
Liderar projetos e iniciativas, assumindo a responsabilidade pelas entregas e coordenando ações com outros times conforme necessário.
Organizar reuniões e sessões de treinamento com stakeholders para alinhar tarefas, solicitar suporte, comunicar melhorias e definir novos processos.
Criar documentações para formalizar melhorias em processos, políticas e outras definições, além de acompanhar projetos e iniciativas em andamento.
Colaborar com diversos times da organização, tanto técnicos quanto não técnicos, para garantir entregas bem-sucedidas.
Desenvolver soluções para aumentar a eficiência dos times operacionais parceiros, otimizando seu tempo e implementando controles para mitigar possíveis erros.
Gerenciar expectativas e contornar objeções de forma eficaz.
viva a missão: inspire e empodere Wellhubbers ao priorizar seu próprio bem-estar e de seus colegas. Faça parte de um ambiente de apoio, onde todas as pessoas se sentem à vontade para cuidar de si mesmas, tirar folgas e encontrar um equilíbrio entre trabalho e vida pessoal.

Residir em São Paulo.
Disponibilidade para comparecer ao escritório quando solicitado.
Conhecimento em Excel.
Capacidade analítica para interpretar dados, extrair insights e elaborar apresentações corporativas.
Perfil proativo, com foco na resolução de problemas e na satisfação da pessoa cliente.
Fortes habilidades de comunicação verbal e escrita, com ótimo relacionamento interpessoal e colaborativo.
Inglês avançado (obrigatório).
Conhecimento em SQL (intermediário/avançado) e ferramentas de BI (Looker, Tableau, Metabase) será um diferencial.
Experiência prévia em mapeamento de processos ou projetos de transformação de negócios será um diferencial.
Experiência em atendimento ao cliente ou operações B2B será um diferencial.

WELLHUB: Plano Gold+ gratuito, com acesso a milhares de academias e estúdios, programas fitness digitais e recursos online para meditação, nutrição, suporte de saúde mental, rotina de sono e mais. Quando você entrar no Wellhub, também pode usar o nosso reembolso de home office para montar o seu escritório em casa!

Queremos que cada pessoa colaboradora possa estar presente de verdade e aproveite esse tempo em família. Por isso, oferecemos licença parental 100% remunerada a todos os novos pais. Quem dá à luz também tem direito à licença estendida (Empresa Cidadã) e a um período de adaptação (ramp-back), em que pode trabalhar meio-período até se ajustar à nova rotina.

No seu estágio, você também vai desenvolver um projeto todo seu, baseado na área e suas especialidades e ter apadrinhamento para ajudar no seu estágio. No Wellhub, a gente foca em aprendizado e feedback contínuos para apoiar seu caminho em direção ao sucesso – tanto pessoal quanto profissional.
CULTURA: Você vai se juntar a uma equipe de pessoas dedicadas, que se unem para romper limites, apoiar umas às outras e criar impacto duradouro no bem-estar corporativo. Nós vencemos em conjunto, cultivando relações de confiança por meio de comunicação transparente e de uma cultura em que cada perspectiva importa. Entenda mais sobre nossos valores e cultura.

MycoSense est une startup technologique suisse en pleine croissance qui révolutionne l'industrie agricole grâce à des solutions avancées de vision par ordinateur, d'intelligence artificielle et d'infrastructures connectées. Nos produits phares (tels que le Spotlight et la VisionBox) sont des systèmes industriels de pointe déployés à l'international.

Pour soutenir notre croissance, nous recherchons une personne clé pour reprendre et diriger nos opérations de production matérielle en qualité de : Responsable de Production & Prototypage Matériel (Hardware Production & Operations Manager) à 100% - CDI.

En tant que Responsable de Production, vous serez le chef d'orchestre de la fabrication de nos équipements. Vous assurerez la transition fluide entre la conception et la livraison du produit final. Vous gérerez l'ensemble du cycle de production, de l'approvisionnement en composants jusqu'à l'expédition chez nos clients, tout en encadrant notre équipe d'assemblage.

· Gestion de la Production : Planifier, superviser et optimiser les cycles de production et d'assemblage de nos systèmes industriels (Spotlights, VisionBoxes, accessoires), en garantissant le respect des délais et des standards de qualité.

· Management d'équipe : Encadrer et soutenir notre technicienne d'assemblage et de contrôle qualité (QA), en assurant une charge de travail équilibrée et des processus fluides.

· Supply Chain & Stocks : Gérer l'inventaire via notre ERP (InvenTree), anticiper les besoins matériels, passer les commandes et maintenir d'excellentes relations avec notre réseau de fournisseurs internationaux (pièces métalliques, impression 3D, électronique/PCBA).

· Contrôle Qualité & Logistique : Superviser les procédures de tests fonctionnels et de QA. Assurer la préparation rigoureuse des produits, leur emballage et la logistique d'expédition vers nos clients à travers le monde.

· Prototypage & R&D (Collaboration transversale) : Travailler en étroite collaboration avec notre équipe d'ingénieurs (logiciel, vision par ordinateur, systèmes embarqués) pour aider au design, au montage et à l'itération rapide de nouveaux prototypes mécaniques et électroniques.

· Expérience exigée : Expérience avérée dans la gestion de production, l'assemblage et la supply chain de machines ou d'équipements industriels intégrant de l'électronique de pointe.

· Langues : Excellente maîtrise de l'anglais (lu, écrit, parlé) impérative. Notre équipe est internationale et une grande partie de notre documentation et de nos communications avec les fournisseurs se fait en anglais. Une bonne maîtrise du français est nécessaire pour les opérations locales.

· Organisation & Rigueur : Excellente capacité à gérer de multiples priorités, à structurer des processus (utilisation d'ERP) et à maintenir une traçabilité parfaite.

· Esprit "Startup" : Vous êtes pragmatique, autonome, capable de prendre des initiatives et n'avez pas peur de "mettre les mains dans le cambouis" sur l'établi quand c'est nécessaire.

· Compétences techniques pratiques pour participer activement au prototypage (connaissances en CAO/CAD mécanique, lecture de schémas électroniques, impression 3D, outillage).

· Expérience préalable avec les procédures douanières et l'expédition internationale de matériel électronique.

· Un rôle central avec de vraies responsabilités au sein d'une entreprise innovante ayant un produit qui a déjà fait ses preuves sur le marché mondial.

· Un environnement de travail dynamique, collaboratif et à la pointe de la technologie.
Lieu : Bourg-en-Lavaux (Cully), Vaud, Suisse
Type de contrat : À temps plein
Veuillez adresser votre dossier de candidature complet (lettre, CV, diplômes et certificats de travail) à l'attention de sd@mycosense.ch.

* Du hast ein gutes Händchen für Kundschaft: Du trittst professionell auf, findest Lösungen und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Aufträge sauber, zuverlässig und zur Zufriedenheit unserer Kundschaft erledigt werden
* Du willst nicht einfach verwalten: Du bringst Ideen ein, entwickelst den Betrieb weiter und machst Albisbrunn als Ausbildungsort jeden Tag ein Stück besser

* Führungserfahrung, Organisationstalent und unternehmerisches Denken gehören zu deinen Stärken

**Das erwartet dich**
* ein traumhaft schöner Arbeitsort
* ein aufgestelltes Team, vielleicht das beste der Welt
* flache Hierarchien
* mind. 5 Wochen Ferien
* ein nicht alltägliches, interessantes Umfeld eines Jugendheims

Health can’t wait .
Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.
Alan exists to end the wait.
Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.
So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.
We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.
Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 800+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.
⭐️ Operations at Alan
The Operations Community’s core responsibilities is to deliver at scale our insurance and health services : we build our platform and operational capabilities and run our processes to guarantee delight and efficiency.
As we anchor our Insurance position, diversify our offering with health and well-being related services in 4 different countries (France, Belgium, Spain and Canada), our operations are increasingly complex and our challenges ahead have never been as exciting!
Being an Ops at Alan means joining a team of 50+ talented, committed and passionate Ops across our countries , with a lot of interactions with Engineering, Product, Care and many other teams at Alan.
We have a mix of Builder profiles, focused on (re)designing and implementing our processes and Operations Coordinators who deliver those on a daily basis while improving them .
We want team members to deliver excellence to our companies and members and be ready to disrupt (and not only upgrade) the way we traditionally think about insurance or healthcare services .
Want to learn more about Ops at Alan? Read how we work and hire and watch our team in action
📍 Join Alan’s Operations team in Lyon
The Operations Coordinator works on a specific subset of services we deliver (eg. claim reimbursement, fraud, clinic to name a few) .

s.h: Their core responsibilities (+- 70/80% of the time) are to
s.t:
Run our Insurance or Health services processes - that's why we call them Ops Runners internally 😉
Ensure the day-to-day follow up and monitoring of our operations
Flag risks and opportunities

Operating our processes: performing tasks like invoicing or claims treatment, growing and managing our network of providers, supporting internal teams (live and through documentation)
Contributing to the definition & owning the best monitoring scheme to track volumes/efficiency/SLAs, and identify risks and areas of improvement, internally or with our service providers
Supervising partnerships (e.g. teleconsultation, claim operators) , participating in the negotiation rounds, daily communication to ensure business continuity
Performing controls on our daily operations to make sure the correct decisions were made and to identify training needs (internally as well as externally)
Escalating feedback, helping to prioritise and supporting initiatives to make our processes and services more delightful and efficient
Next to running and monitoring our operations, you implement continuous improvements to our processes (+-20/30% of the time) . This can be in a variety of ways, e.g. working with product teams to automate certain processes, enhancing our external communication, auditing our processes, automating some process steps using automation tools, …
⭐️ Our Run organisation ⭐️
Our Operations Coordinators or Ops Runners are organized in pools (3-7 runners) who are collectively responsible for running their scope. Examples of topics are:
Alan therapy: members can book a therapy session with psychologists. You maintain smooth relationships with our psychologists, ensure therapy demand matches the supply and contribute to several steps of their lifecycle at Alan (hiring, onboarding, invoicing, supporting booking management etc).
Claims: We provide a best-in-class claims experience, including our own optic care service. You treat claims and assist in decisions regarding our coverage. Additionally, you monitor the performance of external service providers to meet SLAs & perform quality controls. You ensure glasses get delivered on time, member satisfaction is high, our frame collection is attractive, collaboration with opticians is smooth and efficient, ….
Fraud: We run checks on claims submitted by our members, and build new ways of preventing fraud attempts. You investigate suspicious claims, prevent fraudulent payments or recover when we paid fraudulent claims.
Set up: We provide best-in-class experience to our Customers : a smooth on/offboarding of their employees and a seamless invoicing or billing. To do so, we continuously control & improve the quality of our processes : ensuring we have consistent information for invoicing, unlocking employee invite/removals in case of issue and supporting admin in case of payment issue or bankruptcy.
Note : We look for profiles able to embrace any challenge and jump in any pool ! Depending on Alan needs (and personal interests), an Operations Coordinator will join in a pool and can change and explore new scopes after some time. Do not hesitate to ask more concrete examples to the Operations Team Members you’ll meet during the process so they can share about their own scope.
⭐️ Experience ⭐️
For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the A2-B1 level range .
Since the scope of our Ops Runner role is extremely varied, we are open to candidates from different backgrounds : you could be a good fit for the Operations team at Alan if, for example, you:
Operated processes and services especially for companies during the scale up stage or in industrial/logistic industries
Worked in Support functions (Customer Support, People Operations etc)
Had a Customer facing Commercial experience, e.g. account manager or Customer Success Communications , such as Social Media, Internal/ External Communications
Handled event coordination
⭐️ Skills ⭐️
Passionate about delivering & optimizing top notch operations: not scared to get your hands dirty to get into technical processes, making them clear and delightful for our operators and members
A keen problem-solver and challenger with a dig deep mindset: what drives you is member and customer satisfaction !
Analytics skills, to be able to dive into our data
Highly organised with exceptional follow-up skills, with strong attention to details
Strong and structured in written and verbal communication in English as well as in French or Dutch
Able to work and learn independently in a fast-paced environment
Adaptable : you show flexibility and a strong ability to adapt to variable situations

About the role LANCH baut Food-Brands für die Delivery- und QSR-Welt. Dafür verbinden wir starke Marken mit exzellenter Operations, Technologie und datenbasierten Entscheidungen.
Als Senior Business Operations Manager sorgst du dafür, dass wichtige Themen nicht bei der Analyse stehen bleiben, sondern umgesetzt werden. Du strukturierst komplexe Herausforderungen, verbesserst Prozesse und führst bereichsübergreifende Projekte von der ersten Idee bis zum messbaren Ergebnis.

Du analysierst Performance-Daten, entwickelst klare Handlungsempfehlungen und übersetzt sie in konkrete Maßnahmen.
Du übernimmst Verantwortung für bereichsübergreifende Projekte, von der Zieldefinition bis zur Umsetzung.
Du verbesserst Prozesse, Strukturen und Verantwortlichkeiten und sorgst dafür, dass Lösungen nachhaltig funktionieren.
Du koordinierst Stakeholder, löst Blocker und hältst wichtige Initiativen konsequent auf Kurs.
Du unterstützt den Launch und die Weiterentwicklung neuer Produkte, Brands, Standorte und Märkte.
Du erkennst sinnvolle Einsatzmöglichkeiten für Automatisierung, AI und neue Tools und treibst deren Einführung pragmatisch voran.
Du hilfst dabei, LANCH mit dem Wachstum skalierbarer und effizienter zu machen.

About Coursera + Udemy
Coursera and Udemy are now one company, bringing together two mission-driven brands to create the world’s most powerful platform for turning learning into progress. Together, we help more than 300 million learners and 12,000+ enterprise customers build the skills they need for a world being reshaped by AI. Read more about the combined company by visiting our blog .

AI is transforming how people learn, work, and grow, and the need for new skills has never been greater. Coursera brings trusted content and credentials from leading university and industry partners, while Udemy brings a dynamic skills marketplace and global network of real-world experts. By combining these strengths, we can connect more people and organizations to the skills they need, when they need them.
Shape what comes next
By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to reshape how the world learns and applies skills—and help millions of people participate in the new economy. Bring your ideas, expertise, and perspective to meaningful work that can make a difference at global scale.
Coursera + Udemy lets you choose the best way to work, whether it’s from home, an office, or a collaboration space. We’re a globally distributed team that comes together intentionally for collaboration, complex problem-solving, and key milestones — creating opportunities for teams to come together. If you’re ready to make a global impact, help scale unique products across Coursera + Udemy, and grow your career, apply below.

Learning Program Management: You know how to keep a learning program running smoothly — maintaining content relevance, managing the moving parts of an existing learning program, and making sure learners continue to get value from what's already been built.
Business Analysis: You can dig into how a customer is using the platform, proactively identify gaps and opportunities, and turn what you find into practical recommendations that make a real difference for their learners and admins.
Stakeholder Management: You build strong working relationships with the people you support — understanding their priorities, communicating clearly, and serving as a reliable, knowledgeable resource they can count on.
Continual Improvement Process: You do not just complete tasks — you look for patterns, spot opportunities to do things better, and proactively suggest improvements that help customers get more value from the platform over time.

The Learning Operations Manager serves as a dedicated operational partner to Udemy Business customers, acting as the specialized "right hand" to the customer's internal platform admin or product owner.

Because that admin is typically managing multiple HR tools, this role goes deeper on Udemy than the customer realistically can — handling day-to-day platform operations, catalog awareness, license management, and lightweight reporting.

This role may support customers through a premium add-on, temporary backfill arrangements, or ongoing admin-style support engagements, providing consistent and proactive platform expertise that helps customers run Udemy more effectively and keep their learners engaged.
What you’ll be doing
Manage day-to-day platform operations including license management and rotation, configuration updates, and learning path upkeep
Draw on deep knowledge of the Udemy catalog to help customers identify relevant content, surface recommendations, and find replacements for retired or outdated material
Deliver lightweight reporting and surface insights to customer admins, including guidance on which metrics to track and what the data means in practice
Chase down open support requests on behalf of customer admins, following up on ticket status and flagging anything that needs attention — routing technical resolution to the appropriate support teams as needed
Facilitate ad hoc training sessions, webinars, and lunch-and-learns to support platform adoption and build administrator confidence
Serve as the customer's go-to Udemy expert, providing deeper platform knowledge than their internal team can sustain across multiple tools
Manage incoming operational requests across a portfolio of customer accounts, triaging and fulfilling tasks with consistency and care
Escalate thoughtfully when requests fall outside the scope of the engagement, routing customers to the right internal teams
What you’ll have
Experience in a platform operations, managed services, learning administration, or customer-facing support role
A strong sense of what good looks like in a learning program — able to evaluate whether content is well-sequenced, paths are logically organized, and programs are set up for learner success
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage tasks and requests across multiple customer accounts simultaneously
Ability to analyze platform usage and engagement data and translate findings into practical, actionable recommendations
Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to build trust with customer admins and keep stakeholders informed and aligned
A proactive mindset — comfortable identifying opportunities for improvement and raising them before customers have to ask
Experience facilitating training sessions, webinars, or other learning events in a professional context
Comfort working across a variety of customer engagements, from premium support arrangements to temporary backfill situations

About Substrate
Substrate is the critical infrastructure layer between AI and biology. AI for biology has a data problem, not a compute problem: biological foundation models can predict but cannot experiment, and the large-scale, high-quality data they need does not exist. We are building the lab that generates it, with quality and provenance built in. We are not a CRO and we are not a cloud lab.
The company was founded by Mostafa ElSayed, co-founder and CEO; Oli Hoy, who leads the lab buildout and operations; Alexey Morgunov, who leads science and intelligence software; and Anna Huyghues-Despointes, who leads partnerships and go-to-market.

You will run the day-to-day operations of our lab in London, and be the person the scientists come to when something is missing, broken, late or lost. The day-one work is what you would expect: consumables and stock, goods in and cold chain, equipment servicing and calibration, suppliers and purchasing, waste streams and safety records.
Three parts go beyond a standard lab operations job. The first is provenance. Every experiment we sell carries a record of what went into it, down to the lot of the consumable used and the conditions material was held in. If a lot number is not captured, the data point is worth less, and that record runs through you.
The second is that the systems are not written yet. Inventory, goods in, asset registers and ordering exist in no form that will survive the next year. You define what the lab has to capture and work with the science and software teams to make sure it does.
The third is that sample handling and stock control here get automated, and you help specify the system that does it. Every sample, plate, reagent and consumable lot carries a barcode, scanned at each point it is handled, so the record is created by the work rather than reconstructed afterwards.

The same scan draws stock down, which turns reordering from a weekly count into something the system flags before anyone is short. Our software team is building that layer now and the requirements have to come from the lab floor: what gets a barcode, where the scan points sit, and what happens when a label will not read.

Some find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing which one you are.
Your first 90 days
First 30 days
Take ownership of goods in: every delivery received, booked in, stored correctly and recorded.
Map how material moves through the lab and build the first accurate picture of what we hold. That map is the input to a fully barcoded scheme and system.
Days 30 to 60
Put a working inventory and reorder system in place, with minimum levels set from real consumption rather than guesses, and own the purchasing loop.
Agree the barcode and labelling scheme with the software team, and get equipment records in one place.
Days 60 to 90
Run the lab as a routine that does not depend on being asked, with the barcoded system live across one workflow, goods-in to bench to stock draw-down, feeding our provenance record.

You have run the physical side of a lab where being out of stock stops the work: biotech, pharma, a university or institute lab, or a manufacturing or diagnostics operation built around one.

Lab consumables and the rhythm of a working lab are already familiar to you, you have handled real volume and real inventory, and you know the difference between a system that works on paper and one that works at eight on a Monday morning.

We are not asking for a particular speciality, but you should arrive able to run the lab rather than learn what one needs.

Two or more years running a lab or comparable physical operation, hands-on and accountable for the result.
Practical stock control: goods in, inventory records, reorder points, stock counts that reconcile.
Buying from suppliers: raising orders, comparing quotes, managing lead times.
Hands-on with a barcoded or scanned stock system, including what goes wrong when people skip the scan.
Lab environment experience: cold storage, hazardous waste, containment, controlled materials.

Health and safety training such as IOSH.
Developed or co-developed a barcode system for autonomous workflows in labs, including working with software development teams to implement it.
How we work and who you will work with
This role is on site five days a week at 20 Triton Street in London, because the lab is a physical place and the work is in it. The wider founding team is distributed across London, New York and Europe.

You will report to Simon Varzandeh, a member of our scientific staff working on protein characterisation and one of the lab's heaviest users, and work alongside the protein science and functional genomics teams, the engineers building the tracking and stock system with you, and operations on facilities, health and safety and purchasing.

You will be the first person here whose whole job is focused on the lab floor.
We work in the open and each person owns their area. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover.

We're looking for a Marketplace Operations Manager II to own visit delivery for a defined set of Wheel's client programs. This is an operator's role for someone who wants day-to-day ownership of critical business outcomes - and can carry that accountability even when some levers live with peer functions.

You'll take on the complex, ambiguous problems that come with scaling a fast-growing telehealth marketplace - from stabilizing a roster through demand volatility, to leading cross-functional projects that shape how Marketplace Operations scales next.
You will own the visit delivery SLA commitments, program-level consult cost performance, and the roster health for your clients. Separate functions on the team own overall clinician supply forecasting, clinician performance management, and scheduling - freeing you up to optimize their use within your programs.
This is a role for someone who wants to run marketplace operations for key clients end-to-end: launching and configuring new client programs, writing the operational playbooks your programs run on, and deploying incentive spend within guardrails - while trusting peer functions to own adjacent responsibilities in order for you to maintain a singular, maniacal focus on client performance.

Program Performance and Delivery
Own marketplace performance outcomes (contractual and otherwise) for your assigned client programs: SLA attainment, program-level clinician pay cost, and roster/staffing health.
Own roster composition and staffing strategy for your programs, building and adjusting rosters to ensure SLA through client growth, churn, and short-term volatility.
Own operational data analytics and reporting for your programs - pulling and interrogating utilization, breach-pattern, and profitability data yourself and turning it into recommendations and actions
Own the operating rhythm and upward performance visibility for your programs: recurring performance reviews of SLA, utilization, and cost that turns into actions.
Partner with the Capacity Planner to understand near-term volatility and how it may affect client demand (ie demand surges, modality changes, etc) and own the operational response for your programs (escalation thresholds, incentive levers, roster mix) to keep the program on track.
Cost and Incentives
Optimize program-level clinician pay cost and deploy consult incentive spend within a defined budget.
Own the cost plan for your programs and be accountable to variance - partner with the Director of Marketplace on expected cost-per-consult, and keep your lever costs calibrated so you know how to deploy your incentives appropriately.
Real-Time Response and Agent Oversight
Author the real-time escalation and response playbook your programs run on: thresholds, approved corrective actions, escalation triggers. Real-time monitoring and AI agents execute against the playbook you write, and you refine how they act on your programs as their capabilities grow.
Review how the agents act on your programs - audit their decisions for quality, catch policy drift or mistakes early, and feed corrections back into the playbook and the agent logic. You're the human-in-the-loop that keeps automated responses trustworthy on your book.
Partner with clinician management peers to relay clinician performance observations that impact your programs and to identify roster improvements that will drive your client performance.
Client Launches and Partnership
Partner with Customer Success as the operational counterpart on the client's commercial relationship - supporting quarterly business reviews and the real-world story behind client performance.
Own launch supply-readiness with Provider Operations and the Capacity Planner - ensuring clinicians are credentialed, licensed, and activated in the right states, at the volume the program needs, before go-live.
Lead new-client implementation - configuration and setup - as part of cross functional onboarding teams, and own expansions for programs you already run.
Support strategic projects across Marketplace Operations as they arise.

An operator with experience working in fast-paced, high-demand environments - someone who digs into the details to find root cause, spots broken or inefficient processes, and builds the fix rather than just flagging the problem.
Experience owning end-to-end operational performance in a marketplace, logistics, or two-sided platform environment (delivery, rideshare, staffing, workforce management) - direct accountability for SLA, throughput, or cost.
Strategic thinker who connects day-to-day program performance to the bigger picture - you can zoom out from a single roster or escalation to spot the pattern worth fixing structurally, and zoom back in to execute it.
A strong cross-functional partner and team player - you know how to work through peer teams and different personalities to drive your program's outcomes, even when you don't own every lever yourself.
Strong data fluency. You pull and interrogate your own SLA, completion, utilization, and cost-to-plan data and drive decisions from it - hands-on with SQL, Looker, and Excel - rather than waiting for someone to translate it for you.
A direct, clear communicator who authors and revises the procedures your programs run on - escalation playbooks, response plans, launch runbooks - rather than only following ones someone else wrote.

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
We assess businesses in minutes and send funds in as little as 24 hours. That only works if the systems behind it are fast, reliable, and built to scale as we push into new markets. Right now, that means untangling recurring problems across Underwriting, Product, and Sales, and building the automations that stop them coming back.
What you'll actually do
Root-cause the recurring problems that slow us down. You'll define your own KPIs, dig into self-sourced data, and take your findings straight to Director and VP-level leadership.
Build automations that solve a whole business domain, not a single ticket. You'll work across Jira, Hubspot, Pipedream, Tines, and Scriptrunner, and you'll own them end to end: scoping, building, testing, launching.
Run cross-functional projects from definition to delivery. You'll own the relationship with teams like Underwriting, Product & Engineering, and Sales globally, and manage dependencies that sit outside your own team.
Find the inefficiencies that span two or more business units before anyone asks you to. You'll help shape the team's roadmap and support teammates as they grow.
Build the AI layer on top of our existing workflows. Using tools like Claude and Tines' AI Agent actions, you'll build them to triage and resolve tickets, speed up routing, and add an intelligence layer on top of existing workflows, extending efforts like our ticket-scoping assistant and fraud-detection agents, not just tinkering alongside them.
What this role could turn into
This function moves people fast. Recent paths from this seat include a Senior Operations Manager role owning a full domain end to end, a Product Ops or Automation Lead role going deeper on the technical build, or a cross-functional leadership role managing a small team of Ops generalists.
Who thrives here
Someone who digs in when something breaks instead of escalating and waiting. You've done your own homework before you ask for help, and when you do ask, you bring options, not just the question. You're relentless about root cause, not just the symptom in front of you. You're sharp on prioritisation.

You know the difference between busy and useful, and you can explain why you said yes, no, or not yet in a way people accept. People also just like working with you. You're generous with your time and knowledge, and people are generous back. You care about diversity, equality, and inclusion, and you say something when we can do better.
We hire for range
You have 4+ years of relevant experience, ideally at a fast-paced start-up or scale-up, and you've owned projects independently end to end.

You can point to real examples of scoping, building, and owning workflow automations end-to-end (Jira, HubSpot, Pipedream, Tines, Scriptrunner or similar), not just supporting them, and of leading cross-functional teams to deliver solutions, including managing stakeholders outside your own team.

Hands-on SQL experience is required, along with knowledge of Python or another scripting language. You've applied AI tools like Claude or Cursor to go from idea to working code or automation, this is a requirement and we do it on a daily basis.

We care more about the trajectory you're on, though experience in financial services, fintech, or B2B is particularly interesting to us.
Location and working policy
📍 Dublin - hybrid (3 days per week in the office)
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and a pension. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
RevOps at Wayflyer is a team of builders. We're not just looking for people who can spot what's broken and flag it, that skill matters and we have great people who do it well. We're looking for people who also have the technical range to build the fix themselves, independently, without waiting on someone else's roadmap.
We sit at the epicenter of an exceptionally fast-growing business running across multiple channels and partners, and it's our job to make sure the systems underneath that growth have the ability to scale. This role is for a builder who wants to see the impact of their work fast, ideally in seconds, while still thinking several steps ahead so today's quick fix doesn't turn into next year's technical debt. We want people who enjoy the instant feedback loop just as much as the long game.
What you'll actually do
Integrations & Technical Ownership: Build, maintain and improve the systems, internal automations and integrations that make our sales and CS teams faster and more effective, from the ground up.
AI-Native Systems: Build, deploy and continuously sharpen AI-native workflows and agents that augment how Sales, CS and the wider Revenue org work, not just automate around the edges.
Data, Analytics & Problem Solving: Use self-sourced data to diagnose what's actually broken, run root cause analysis, and build the fix yourself, then measure it against real KPIs and keep iterating.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Project Ownership: Work directly with Sales, Partnerships, Marketing and Finance to turn half-formed requirements into systems that actually solve the problem.
Revenue Data Hygiene: Own regular audits, deduplication, enrichment and the process fixes that keep our data usable across every system that touches it.
Driving Operational Excellence: Spot inefficiencies before anyone asks you to, prioritise ruthlessly, and build the automated solutions that let the function scale without adding headcount.
What this role could turn into
This function sits at the intersection of Revenue, Marketing, Finance, Data and Engineering, so you'll get exposure most people spend years angling for. People who do this well tend to move toward GTM strategy, GTM engineering, product roles, and beyond. The sky is the limit.
Who thrives here
You're an AI-native builder who thinks in scale, not one-off fixes, and gets uncomfortable when you spot a manual workaround. You're just as comfortable pairing with Engineering as you are in the room with Sales leadership, translating one for the other without losing anything in the middle.

You run towards the hardest, messiest problems, you don't wait for permission, and you don't need a fully-scoped brief before you start. You're always watching what the best GTM teams are building, and you'd rather pitch a bold idea than ship another incremental tweak.
We hire for range
3+ years in RevOps, MarOps, consulting or similar, but tenure isn't the point, trajectory is. Whatever your background, you're an AI-native builder with strong business acumen and a sharp eye for the difference between a good customer experience and a bad one.
You bring fluency in Python (or Node) and SQL, hands-on experience configuring HubSpot and its developer suite, and comfort with automation platforms like Zapier, Pipedream, n8n or UiPath.

You've likely configured CPQ, CLM, sales engagement or customer-success platforms before, and just as importantly, you've driven adoption of something you built, not just shipped it and walked away. Extra credit if you've built and deployed AI agents, integrated AI/LLM-based solutions into existing workflows, or built automated pipelines end to end.
Location and working policy
📍 Dublin or London, Hybrid
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and pension. Equity, because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

Payments at Gusto aren't just infrastructure — they're the reason people get paid on time, every time. Payment Operations sits within Gusto's Money team, a cross-functional group spanning Engineering, Product, and Operations that powers money movement across Gusto's growing product surface: core payroll, contractor payments, international money movement, and new business offerings like PEO.
As a Payment Operations Analyst, you'll own specific end-to-end payment workflows, resolve exceptions that require real judgment, and help make our systems more reliable and efficient over time. Gusto's payment surface area is expanding — and this team is at the center of that growth.
This is a role for someone who can shift from investigating a single misfired transaction to coordinating a response on a payment outage affecting thousands — and bring the same rigor to both. You think in systems. You hold partners accountable. You lead with curiosity and embrace AI as a core part of how you work.
You'll collaborate closely with Engineering, Product, Accounting, Risk, and CX — and you'll develop strong day-to-day relationships with Gusto's bank and payment partners. When something breaks or slows down, you're the one who drives it to resolution.

Support the payment lifecycle end-to-end
Own the operational layer of specific payment workflows — ACH processing, exception handling, refunds, collection re-debits, reconciliation. When something is off, you investigate, escalate where needed, and see it through to resolution. And when you see a pattern, you push to fix the root cause.
Build alongside Product and Engineering
Payment Operations doesn't just react — we shape how the systems work. You'll contribute to product specs, surface operational pain points, help define requirements, and participate in launches. You're a partner in building, not just a consumer of what gets shipped.
Close the loop on customer pain
Customer and CX feedback is signal. You actively mine it to identify friction in payment flows, prioritize what matters, and bring those insights into the operational and product conversations where decisions get made.
Think in systems
Connect the dots across rails, partners, reconciliation, compliance, and customer experience. When an issue surfaces, you understand how it ripples — and you bring that perspective to cross-functional conversations.
Hold partners to a high standard
Work directly with Gusto's bank and payment partners — domestic and international — to triage issues, resolve escalations, and maintain strong working relationships. You know how to be firm and collaborative at the same time, and you don't let things sit.
Lead with AI
You use AI as a genuine work partner — to move faster on analysis, draft communications, synthesize data, and automate the repetitive. You're always looking for the smarter way to get to the answer.

3+ years of experience in payment operations, banking operations, treasury operations, or a related role at a fintech or financial institution
Working knowledge of domestic payment rails (ACH/Nacha, wires, RTP) and/or international money movement (cross-border transfers, FX, global disbursement networks); experience across both is a strong plus
Strong analytical instincts — you look for the pattern behind the problem and can query or structure data to find it (SQL a plus but not required)
Experience working with bank portals, payment processors, or reconciliation tools
Ability to communicate clearly with both operational and technical counterparts; you can write a crisp Slack to an engineer and a professional escalation to a bank partner
Comfortable working in ambiguity and taking ownership without waiting for perfect information
Eager to build AI into how you work — whether you're already using it daily or just getting started, you see it as a genuine productivity lever and are committed to developing that fluency
Knowledge of relevant compliance frameworks (Nacha operating rules, unclaimed property, money transmission) is a strong plus

We are looking for a Chief of Staff–style operator to serve as the President’s right hand and help run, maintain, and continuously evolve the Product, Engineering & Design operating model and cadence.
This role will turn strategy into a durable execution system. You will own the connective tissue across the President’s leadership cadence: preparing the right inputs, creating clarity on decisions and tradeoffs, ensuring commitments are followed through, surfacing risks early, and improving the operating model as the organization changes.

You will work across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Finance, People, and your peers in Business Operations, partnering with senior leaders who do not report to you and influencing through judgment, trust, and clarity.
The successful candidate will combine executive judgment, operational rigor, business acumen, comfort with ambiguity, strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to move fluidly between strategic questions and the execution details required to make the system work.
AI fluency is an important part of this role. You will use approved enterprise AI tools, including tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable platforms, to automate repeatable operating work, synthesize information across functions, improve leadership preparation, surface risks and dependencies, and accelerate strategic-initiative delivery.
This role reports to the VP of Operations at Squarespace and is based remotely in California or locally at our New York City headquarters.
You’ll Get To…
Run the President's operating cadence . Own end-to-end orchestration of the leadership rhythm: staff meetings, WBRs, MBRs, and QBRs, finance and portfolio reviews, priority updates, and annual operating-plan inputs. Ensure each ritual has a clear purpose, owner, input, output, decision authority, and downstream cascade.
Drive decision quality. Synthesize diverse inputs into concise narratives that make priorities, risks, options, tradeoffs, and recommended decisions clear to the President and leadership team. Document decisions in the room, assign owners and deadlines, track commitments, and escalate unresolved issues with context and a proposed path forward.
Improve execution velocity. Identify alignment and execution risks before they surface as leadership surprises, and facilitate resolution across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Customer Operations, Finance, People, and Business Operations, connecting planning, performance, financial, organizational, and roadmap inputs. Use AI and advanced tooling to make decisions faster and better-informed.
Evolve the operating model. Treat the operating system as a living thing. Establish health measures such as decision latency, action closure, cascade reach, pre-read quality, participation, recurring issue themes, and use them to assess whether rituals, artifacts, and escalation paths are producing the right outcomes.

Recommend and implement changes to cadence, governance, templates, roles, and channels as strategy and priorities evolve, codifying what works so the model is easy for leaders to understand and operate.
Lead high-priority strategic initiatives. Drive complex, ambiguous, cross-functional work on behalf of the President, from framing and workplan through decision, implementation, and follow-through, including emerging problems that don't yet have a clear owner. Support annual strategy, goals, headcount, and budget processes by connecting them to the department's operating rhythm.
Represent the President and build transparency. Stand in for the President in meetings, events, and discussions, exercising the remit of the position. Navigate difficult conversations and cross-functional tradeoffs without relying on formal authority. Support two-way access to the President through Town Halls, Roundtables, Office Hours, and written follow-up, using sound judgment about what should be broadly communicated, selectively shared, or handled privately.
Serve as a trusted thought partner to the President and senior leadership team, offering an independent perspective and respectfully challenging assumptions when needed.

Significant experience in Chief of Staff, Product Operations, Business Operations, Strategy & Operations, or management consulting
A track record of owning an operating model, leadership cadence, or portfolio of complex cross-functional initiatives, preferably in tech companies
Knowledge of the product / software development lifecycle
Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable approved tools, and experience integrating them into daily workflows to automate repeatable tasks, optimize processes, improve synthesis, and accelerate project delivery.
Exceptional written communication: you can turn a large volume of input into a concise, decision-ready narrative tailored to the audience
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand metrics, forecasts, resource tradeoffs, product or portfolio performance, and organizational implications.
Strong executive presence and facilitation skills; you can create clarity and momentum in high-stakes or ambiguous settings.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, build consensus, resolve conflict, and push for decisions without formal authority.
High judgment and discretion when handling sensitive organizational, people, financial, and strategic information.
Comfort operating in ambiguity, switching between strategic altitude and detailed execution, and taking ownership of problems that cross organizational boundaries.
A continuous-improvement mindset: you distinguish between process and content, challenge ineffective routines, and make change practical and durable.
A bias toward action, paired with the judgment to know when to decide, when to seek input, and when to escalate.
What Success Looks Like

s.h: In the first 6–12 months, you will
s.t:
Implement a dependable operating rhythm in which leadership forums are well-prepared, decision-oriented, and followed through.
Improve the quality and consistency of pre-reads, decision logs, action tracking, portfolio updates, and quarterly communications.
Make it easy to see what changed, what matters now, what decisions are needed, who owns the next step, and where risk is accumulating.
Establish a small number of reliable AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual preparation and reporting effort, improve the timeliness and quality of leadership inputs, and make follow-through more visible.
Increase the organization’s ability to reuse knowledge, detect recurring issues, and move from raw information to clear decisions without adding unnecessary process.
Build strong working relationships and trust with the President and his leaders across the department and company, leading with tact, discretion and respect.
Help the President and leadership team make faster, clearer, better-informed decisions without adding unnecessary processes or meetings.
Leave the system more scalable and more resilient than you found it.

You’ll be joining a team that delivers high‑quality e‑commerce data across more than 40 countries. We’re looking for a detail‑oriented, analytically minded Data Operations Analyst to be part of our dynamic, multicultural team. In this role, you’ll contribute to the entire data operations lifecycle—from validating, extracting, and processing digital transaction data to troubleshooting data quality issues and partnering with cross‑functional teams.
This is a great opportunity for early‑career professionals eager to build a solid foundation in data analysis within a client‑focused environment. You’ll also have the chance to drive new initiatives and continuous improvements.

If you enjoy solving puzzles, you’ll feel right at home: your logical thinking and analytical mindset will help you navigate complex challenges, identify patterns, and uncover insights. With constant learning at the core of this role, curiosity and ownership will be essential to your success.

Data Extraction
Build data extractors to parse e-receipts using NielsenIQ’s proprietary markup language and RegEx.
Debug and fine-tune templates to make sure they’re accurate, then validate your work with SQL and BI tools.
Keep documentation clear and communicate effectively with tech teams and client-facing teams.
Adapt extraction logic as data formats and business needs change.
Stay up to date with our internal processes and tools.
Data Quality & Analysis
Conduct comprehensive checks to ensure data is complete, accurate, consistent, and correctly parsed, leveraging BI tools and SQL.
Investigate anomalies and irregularities specific to transactional data.
Write and optimize SQL queries, and build dashboards to support large‑scale analysis.
Prepare clear, actionable reports for client‑facing teams.
Process Improvement
Spot opportunities for automation and help improve our processes and tools.
Support strategic projects aimed at improving operational workflows.
Work closely with developers, analysts and client-facing teams to design solutions together.
Keep operational and project documentation up to date.

First experience (internship, projects) in data operations, analytics or tech related roles.
Basic SQL skills: Ability to write simple queries to retrieve and inspect data; Can read and understand more complex queries written by others; Understands table structures, relationships, and how data is organized within a database.
A logical, analytical mindset to tackle complex tasks and spot patterns in data.
Great communication skills and attention to detail (crucial when working with data that people rely on to make decisions).
Fluency in English.

Hands-on experience with at least one BI tool like Tableau, Power BI, Looker etc.
Knowledge of e-commerce data and industry trends.
Familiarity with analytical platforms like Snowflake or Databricks.
Previous experience in QA or data validation.
Familiarity with HTML, XML, RegEx, or other scripting/markup languages.
Experience working in agile environments and understanding basic software development processes.
